title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates its experimental applicability on a trapped-ion system.
motivation: Distinguishing projective from non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks that require non-projective measurements, but existing certification methods were incomplete or not robust.
method: They develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy that provides necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a projective simulation, and implement it in an experiment.
result: They certify non-projective measurements in a trapped-ion experiment, proving the impossibility of explaining the data with projective measurements.
conclusion: This provides a robust and complete framework for certifying non-projective measurements, with practical applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantifying Entanglement In Quantum Thermodynamics Via Separability Constraints
authors: Joan Alba, Laura Ares, Jan Sperling, And Julien Pinske
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Alba, Laura Ares, Jan Sperling, and Julien Pinske

The role of quantum entanglement in thermodynamical systems remains elusive. Does entanglement result in thermodynamic advantages or does it impose fundamental limitations? Here, we unambiguously quantify the amount of heat and work in a quantum system that is due to the presence of entanglement. Th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024157] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to quantify the heat and work contributions specifically attributable to quantum entanglement in thermodynamic systems, using separability constraints.
motivation: The role of entanglement in thermodynamics is unclear; the authors aim to provide an unambiguous quantification of entanglement's effect on thermodynamic variables.
method: They employ separability constraints to decompose thermodynamic quantities into entangled and non-entangled contributions, likely using entanglement measures and thermodynamic formalism.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the entangled contributions to heat and work, allowing for a clear separation of entanglement's impact.
conclusion: The work clarifies how entanglement can either provide advantages or impose limitations in thermodynamic processes, offering a framework for understanding quantum thermal machines.

title: Metropolitan Entanglement Distribution Between An Atom And A Near-Visible Photon
authors: Maya Büki, Pooja Malik, Florian Fertig, Tobias Frank, Marvin Scholz, Tommy Block, Gianvito Chiarella, Yiru Zhou, Emanuele Distante, Pau Farrera, Gerhard Rempe, And Harald Weinfurter
abstract:
Author(s): Maya Büki, Pooja Malik, Florian Fertig, Tobias Frank, Marvin Scholz, Tommy Block, Gianvito Chiarella, Yiru Zhou, Emanuele Distante, Pau Farrera, Gerhard Rempe, and Harald Weinfurter

Entanglement distribution is the overarching purpose of quantum networks. While communication over long distances can use deployed fiber infrastructure, it requires photons in the telecom band. However, advanced quantum network nodes do not operate at such wavelengths. Here we overcome this limitati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090803] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates metropolitan-scale entanglement distribution between an atom and a near-visible photon, overcoming telecom wavelength mismatch.
motivation: Quantum networks need long-distance entanglement distribution, but advanced quantum nodes operate at non-telecom wavelengths, requiring solutions for fiber compatibility.
method: The experiment likely uses an atomic quantum memory and a near-visible photon, possibly with frequency conversion to telecom band for transmission over metropolitan fiber, then verifies entanglement.
result: Successful entanglement distribution over metropolitan distances, showing compatibility of atomic nodes with deployed fiber infrastructure.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum networks by enabling metropolitan-scale entanglement distribution with atom-photon interfaces.

title: Fundamental Limits On Polarization Entanglement Distribution In Optical Fiber
authors: Stefano Pirandola
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pirandola

Characterizing the ultimate rates of entanglement distribution is essential for both foundational research and the practical deployment of quantum technologies. To investigate these limits, we introduce an erasure-Pauli channel model describing the distribution of polarization entanglement in optica…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033222] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an erasure-Pauli channel model to characterize fundamental limits on polarization entanglement distribution in optical fiber.
motivation: Understanding the ultimate rates of entanglement distribution is crucial for both foundational research and practical deployment of quantum technologies.
method: The author introduces an erasure-Pauli channel model for polarization entanglement distribution in optical fiber and analyzes its fundamental limits.
result: The paper derives ultimate rates for entanglement distribution in optical fiber.
conclusion: These fundamental limits provide essential bounds for the design and deployment of quantum networks.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that non-Abelian topological order enables the implementation of topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy in a constant-depth, local two-dimensional setup.
motivation: Achieving universal fault-tolerant quantum computation requires logical gates beyond the Clifford group; the Clifford hierarchy provides a framework, but implementing higher-level gates is challenging.
method: The authors employ non-Abelian surface codes and exploit the properties of non-Abelian anyons to construct logical gates at arbitrary levels of the Clifford hierarchy with constant circuit depth.
result: The work shows that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.
conclusion: This result extends the capabilities of topological quantum computation and offers a systematic approach to implementing higher-level Clifford gates, potentially improving schemes for universal quantum computing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum-particle-detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: To understand the fundamental thermodynamic constraints on information acquisition in quantum detectors, and to assess the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of measurement processes.
method: The authors introduce a minimal quantum-particle-detector model and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, focusing on entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that more accurate measurements require higher thermodynamic costs.
conclusion: The results highlight fundamental limits on the accuracy of quantum measurements due to thermodynamic constraints, advancing our understanding of the interplay between information and thermodynamics.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified, operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, directly quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: To develop a rigorous and practical measure of non-Gaussianity that captures the resource cost in continuous-variable quantum information, beyond existing ad hoc quantifiers.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank via symplectic geometry and prove its properties, relating it to state preparation, compression, and measurement costs in bosonic systems.
result: They show the symplectic rank unifies and clarifies non-Gaussianity, providing tight bounds on the resources needed for key quantum information tasks.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful resource measure for non-Gaussian states, likely becoming a standard tool in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Entanglement Certification And Entropy Bounds In The Asymmetric Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Scenario
authors: Xingyuan Bu, Xin Kuang, And Yunguang Han
abstract:
Author(s): Xingyuan Bu, Xin Kuang, and Yunguang Han

Motivated by device-independent quantum information protocols, we study a class of marginal-free asymmetric Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) expressions in which Alice's two measurement settings carry different weights. For [MATH], within the two-qubit projective-measurement model, we derive a …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022620] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: 该论文在不对称CHSH场景下研究了纠缠认证和熵界，为设备无关量子信息协议提供了理论工具。
motivation: 设备无关量子信息协议需要可靠地认证纠缠和量化熵，而标准CHSH不等式假设对称设置，实际场景可能存在不对称性。
method: 论文聚焦于两比特投影测量模型，推导了不对称CHSH表达式下的纠缠认证条件和熵界。
result: 得到了不对称CHSH表达式的纠缠认证准则和相关的熵界，扩展了设备无关协议的理论基础。
conclusion: 该研究深化了对不对称CHSH场景的理解，有助于设计更灵活的设备无关协议。

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates single erbium emitters in silicon coupled to cavities to understand spectral instability and decoherence, which are critical for quantum networking and computation.
motivation: Spectral instability of single-photon emitters is a major barrier to their practical use in quantum networks; identifying its physical origins is essential for developing stable quantum nodes.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, using techniques such as photoluminescence and spectral measurements to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They reveal the origins of spectral instability and decoherence in these systems, providing a detailed understanding of the underlying physics.
conclusion: The insights gained enable strategies to mitigate spectral instability, improving the viability of erbium-based emitters for quantum networking and computation.

title: Mixed-dimensional Quantum MacWilliams Identity: Bounds For Codes And Absolutely Maximally Entangled States In Heterogeneous Systems
authors: David González-Lociga And Simeon Ball
abstract:
Author(s): David González-Lociga and Simeon Ball

As emerging quantum architectures evolve into heterogeneous networks combining different physical substrates, such as qubits for logic and higher-dimensional qudits for robust communication, the traditional scalar metrics of quantum error correction become insufficient. To address this, we introduce…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022464] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a mixed-dimensional quantum MacWilliams identity that yields bounds on quantum codes and absolutely maximally entangled states in heterogeneous systems.
motivation: Heterogeneous quantum networks combining qubits and higher-dimensional qudits require new error-correction metrics beyond scalar approaches.
method: Generalizes the classical MacWilliams identity to mixed-dimensional quantum codes, connecting weight enumerators and using them to derive bounds on code parameters and entanglement properties.
result: Provides new bounds on quantum codes and conditions for existence of absolutely maximally entangled states in mixed-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The identity offers a unified framework for analyzing quantum error correction and entanglement in heterogeneous quantum architectures, advancing quantum information theory.

title: Matrix Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For non-Abelian Charge Transport
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound current precision by entropy production, but transport of noncommuting (non-Abelian) charges lacks a single joint classical record of all current components. We derive an operational, process-level matrix TUR for this setting from the entropy producti…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022106] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Derives a process-level matrix thermodynamic uncertainty relation for non-Abelian charge transport, bounding current precision by entropy production.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) typically apply to systems with a single joint classical current record, but non-Abelian charges lack such a record, necessitating an extension.
method: The paper derives an operational, process-level matrix TUR from entropy production, adapting the framework to handle noncommuting charges.
result: Provides a matrix inequality linking the covariance of non-Abelian currents to entropy production, generalizing standard TURs.
conclusion: Extends thermodynamic uncertainty relations to non-Abelian settings, offering new bounds for quantum transport processes and insights into precision-entropy trade-offs.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a versatile framework that connects layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics to enable realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits.
motivation: To accurately model driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions, which is crucial for designing and optimizing microwave control of superconducting qubits.
method: The framework systematically constructs time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits by bridging microwave simulations and quantum dynamics.
result: The framework enables realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits, improving predictions of qubit behavior and control.
conclusion: The method provides a systematic tool for designing and optimizing microwave-driven superconducting circuits, advancing the hybrid quantum systems field.

title: Equivalence Of Stabilizer And Shannon Reńyi Entropies: Exact Results For Quantum Critical Chains
authors: E. A. Ramirez Trino And M. A. Rajabpour
abstract:
Author(s): E. A. Ramirez Trino and M. A. Rajabpour

Shannon-Rényi and stabilizer entropies are key diagnostics of structure, “nonstabilizerness,” phase transitions, and universality in quantum many-body states. We establish an exact correspondence for quadratic fermions: for any Gaussian eigenstate, the stabilizer Rényi entropy equals the Shannon-Rén…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090403] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that for quadratic fermionic Gaussian states, the stabilizer Rényi entropy exactly equals the Shannon-Rényi entropy, establishing a direct correspondence between these measures in quantum critical chains.
motivation: To understand the relationship between stabilizer entropy, which measures nonstabilizerness, and Shannon-Rényi entropy, which measures structure, and to provide exact results for many-body systems.
method: By analyzing Gaussian states of quadratic fermions and leveraging their properties to derive an exact equivalence between the two entropy measures.
result: For any Gaussian eigenstate, the stabilizer Rényi entropy equals the Shannon-Rényi entropy, meaning the two quantities are exactly the same for these states.
conclusion: This equivalence provides a new tool for studying nonstabilizerness in fermionic systems and may aid in detecting phase transitions and universality in quantum critical chains.

title: Uncovering Hidden Entanglement In Twin Beams
authors: R. L. Rincón Celis, G. Nirala, A. Montaña Guerrero, T. L. Meireles, P. Nussenzveig, M. Martinelli, A. M. Marino, And H. M. Florez
abstract:
Author(s): R. L. Rincón Celis, G. Nirala, A. Montaña Guerrero, T. L. Meireles, P. Nussenzveig, M. Martinelli, A. M. Marino, and H. M. Florez

Proper characterization of quantum correlations in multimode optical quantum states is critical for applications in quantum information science. However, standard entanglement measurements can lead to incomplete state reconstruction and characterization. Here, we implement a resonator-based detectio…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090201] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: 本文通过谐振器基检测方法揭示了双光束中隐藏的纠缠，实现了对多模光学量子态的完整表征。
motivation: 标准纠缠测量可能不完整，导致对多模光学量子态的刻画不充分。
method: 实现了一种基于谐振器的检测方案，用于提取被标准方法忽略的纠缠信息。
result: 成功揭示了双光束中隐藏的纠缠，表明该方案能够提供更完整的量子关联信息。
conclusion: 该工作为多模量子态的表征提供了新工具，对量子信息应用有重要意义。

title: Advantage Framework For Resource Engines
authors: Jakub Czartowski And Rafał Bistroń
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Czartowski and Rafał Bistroń

Thermal engines have been one of the principal topics of thermodynamics ever since its beginning. Today, in the era of the second quantum revolution, although the thermal processes in constant temperatures are relatively well understood in the language of resource theories, a framework to describe t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022461] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general framework for resource engines, which are devices that extract work from quantum resources, unifying and extending existing resource-theoretic approaches to thermodynamics.
motivation: Thermal engines are central to thermodynamics, but current resource theories primarily treat constant temperature processes; a unified framework for engines operating under arbitrary resource constraints is missing.
method: The authors develop an 'advantage framework' that characterizes engines by their ability to convert resources into work, using tools from quantum resource theories and thermodynamics, such as free operations and monotones.
result: The framework provides a general way to evaluate the performance and efficiency of resource engines, recovering standard results and enabling the study of engines beyond thermal equilibrium.
conclusion: This work offers a comprehensive theoretical basis for resource engines, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: General Quantum Resources Providing Advantages In Work-extraction Tasks
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh And Manuel Gessner
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh and Manuel Gessner

In developing quantum science and technologies, it is essential to demonstrate so-called quantum advantages, which are performances that can be achieved only with the assistance of quantum resources. Most of the time, different quantum features lead to different advantages. Interestingly, there are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022456] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how general quantum resources can provide advantages in work-extraction tasks, contributing to quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To identify which quantum features enable quantum advantages in thermodynamic tasks such as work extraction.
method: Proposes a resource-theoretic framework to characterize and quantify the role of different quantum resources in work extraction.
result: Shows that certain quantum resources lead to enhanced work extraction compared to classical or separable operations.
conclusion: Provides a general understanding of how quantum resources can be harnessed for thermodynamic advantages, with implications for quantum technologies.

title: Complex Heat Capacity As A Witness Of Spatio-temporal Entanglement
authors: Mia Stamatova And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Mia Stamatova and Vlatko Vedral

We propose a witness of temporal quantum entanglement using the imaginary component of the complex heat capacity—a measurable thermodynamic quantity in temperature-modulated calorimetry. By establishing a direct correspondence between complex heat capacity and the pseudodensity matrix formalism, our…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022448] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the imaginary component of complex heat capacity as a witness for spatio-temporal quantum entanglement, linking thermodynamics to quantum information detection.
motivation: To provide a measurable thermodynamic quantity that can detect quantum entanglement, specifically temporal entanglement, which is not directly accessible via standard measurement techniques.
method: The authors establish a direct correspondence between complex heat capacity and the pseudodensity matrix formalism, enabling the use of temperature-modulated calorimetry data for entanglement detection.
result: The imaginary component of complex heat capacity is shown to act as an entanglement witness, capable of revealing spatio-temporal quantum correlations.
conclusion: This work introduces a novel thermodynamic approach to witnessing quantum entanglement, highlighting the informational content in thermodynamic observables.

title: Hamiltonian Benchmark Of A Solid-state Spin-photon Interface For Computation
authors: Tejas Acharya, Loïc Lanco, Olivier Krebs, Hui Khoon Ng, Alexia Auffèves, And Maria Maffei
abstract:
Author(s): Tejas Acharya, Loïc Lanco, Olivier Krebs, Hui Khoon Ng, Alexia Auffèves, and Maria Maffei

Quantum interfaces are a cornerstone of photonic quantum computing protocols. They consist of quantum emitters coupled to propagating light pulses, enabling the reversible transfer of information between emitter degrees of freedom, such as energy or spin, and photonic degrees of freedom, including p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115306] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks a solid-state spin-photon interface by analyzing its Hamiltonian, providing insights for photonic quantum computing.
motivation: Spin-photon interfaces are essential for photonic quantum computing, but a systematic benchmark of their Hamiltonian is lacking.
method: The authors construct a Hamiltonian model for the interface and analyze its properties to assess computational performance.
result: The benchmark reveals the interface's capabilities and limitations for quantum information transfer and computation.
conclusion: The Hamiltonian benchmark provides a valuable framework for evaluating and optimizing spin-photon interfaces in quantum computing.

title: Strong Violation Of The Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation In A Minimal Autonomous Heat Engine
authors: Enrique P. Cital And Viktor Holubec
abstract:
Author(s): Enrique P. Cital and Viktor Holubec

Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) impose a universal trade-off between current precision and entropy production in autonomous steady states, constraining in particular the power, efficiency, and constancy of heat engines. We demonstrate strong violations of the long-time TUR in a minimal au…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024153] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates strong violations of the thermodynamic uncertainty relation in a minimal autonomous heat engine, challenging universal trade-offs between precision and entropy production.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations impose trade-offs between current precision and entropy production, constraining heat engine performance. The authors investigate whether these bounds hold universally for minimal autonomous heat engines.
method: They analyze a minimal autonomous heat engine model and compute the long-time TUR, studying conditions under which it is violated.
result: They find strong violations of the long-time TUR, showing that precision can be achieved with lower entropy production than expected.
conclusion: The results indicate that TURs are not universally valid even in simple autonomous heat engines, impacting theoretical constraints on engine performance.

title: Scalable Fluxonium-transmon Architecture For Error-corrected Quantum Processors
authors: Lukas Heunisch, Longxiang Huang, Timo Eckstein, Stephan Tasler, Johannes Schirk, Florian Wallner, Verena Feulner, Bijita Sarma, Klaus Liegener, Christian M. F. Schneider, Stefan Filipp, And Michael J. Hartmann
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Heunisch, Longxiang Huang, Timo Eckstein, Stephan Tasler, Johannes Schirk, Florian Wallner, Verena Feulner, Bijita Sarma, Klaus Liegener, Christian M. F. Schneider, Stefan Filipp, and Michael J. Hartmann

We propose a hybrid quantum computing architecture composed of alternating fluxonium and transmon qubits, which are coupled via transmon tunable couplers. We show that this system offers excellent scaling properties, characterized by engineered zero [MATH] crosstalk in the idle regime, a substantial r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033245] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scalable hybrid architecture combining fluxonium and transmon qubits with tunable couplers to reduce crosstalk for error-corrected quantum processors.
motivation: To address scalability challenges in superconducting quantum processors by designing an architecture with reduced crosstalk and improved qubit performance for fault-tolerant computing.
method: Interleaves fluxonium and transmon qubits coupled via transmon tunable couplers, engineered to achieve zero crosstalk in idle regime and improve scaling.
result: Demonstrates excellent scaling properties and reduced crosstalk, potentially enabling larger error-corrected quantum processors.
conclusion: The architecture offers a promising path toward scalable quantum computing with error correction.

title: Spin Amplification In Realistic Systems
authors: Ivan Iakoupov, Victor M. Bastidas, Yuichiro Matsuzaki, Shiro Saito, And William J. Munro
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Iakoupov, Victor M. Bastidas, Yuichiro Matsuzaki, Shiro Saito, and William J. Munro

Spin amplification is the process that ideally increases the number of excited spins when one of them is excited initially. We show that by applying optimal control techniques to design classical drive pulse shapes, spin amplification can be achieved in a previously unexplored fast regime, with ampl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033227] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates spin amplification in a fast regime using optimal control techniques, enhancing the number of excited spins from a single initial excitation.
motivation: Spin amplification is critical for quantum information processing, but previous methods are slow; the authors aim to achieve it more rapidly.
method: Optimal control techniques are applied to design classical drive pulse shapes for the spin ensemble.
result: Spin amplification is achieved in a previously unexplored fast regime, with improved amplification performance.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables faster spin amplification, potentially benefiting quantum memories and transduction applications.

title: Security-rate Trade-off In Quantum Key Distribution: From Individual Links To Large-scale Networks
authors: Stefano Pirandola, Cillian Harney, And Gaetana Spedalieri
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pirandola, Cillian Harney, and Gaetana Spedalieri

We explore the interplay between security and key rate of a quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol. This fundamental trade-off is investigated both at the link layer, i.e., for a QKD protocol implemented on a channel, and at the network layer, i.e., within the context of a multiuser multihop commun…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033221] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically analyzes the trade-off between security and key rate in QKD, covering both individual links and large-scale network architectures.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental security-rate trade-off is crucial for designing efficient and secure QKD systems, especially when scaling to multiuser networks.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds and relationships between security parameters and achievable key rates, using information-theoretic and optimization techniques across link and network layers.
result: They provide quantitative characterizations of the security-rate trade-off, revealing fundamental limits and optimal strategies for QKD links and networks.
conclusion: The findings offer practical guidance for balancing security and performance in QKD deployment, informing the design of scalable and secure quantum networks.

title: Broken Detailed Balance And Entropy Production In Completely Positive And Trace-preserving Quantum Brownian Motion
authors: Simone Artini, Gabriele Lo Monaco, Alberto Imparato, Mauro Paternostro, And Sandro Donadi
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Artini, Gabriele Lo Monaco, Alberto Imparato, Mauro Paternostro, and Sandro Donadi

We rigorously analyze the nonequilibrium thermodynamic behavior of various formulations of quantum Brownian motion using the framework of stochastic thermodynamics. While the widely used Caldeira-Leggett master equation exhibits desirable thermodynamic features—such as the fulfillment of a detailed …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033216] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously analyzes the nonequilibrium thermodynamic behavior of quantum Brownian motion, focusing on detailed balance and entropy production under completely positive and trace-preserving dynamics.
motivation: The commonly used Caldeira-Leggett master equation satisfies detailed balance, but it is unclear if other formulations do, and how entropy production relates to this. Understanding these properties is crucial for applying stochastic thermodynamics to open quantum systems.
method: The authors compare several master equation formulations for quantum Brownian motion within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, examining the validity of detailed balance and computing entropy production rates.
result: They find that some formulations violate detailed balance, leading to differences in entropy production, and they clarify the conditions under which a consistent thermodynamic interpretation is possible.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous thermodynamic assessment of different quantum Brownian motion models, offering guidance for choosing appropriate master equations in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics applications.

title: Revealing The Nonclassicality Of A Molecular Nanomagnet
authors: Alessandra Cammarata, Steve Campbell, And Mauro Paternostro
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Cammarata, Steve Campbell, and Mauro Paternostro

Molecular nanomagnets are compounds characterized by a high-spin magnetic core that is protected by organic ligands. They have recently gained attention as potential quantum information carriers in solid-state quantum computing platforms, simultaneously exhibiting classical macroscopic properties an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033207] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the nonclassical nature of molecular nanomagnets, demonstrating their potential as quantum information carriers.
motivation: Molecular nanomagnets are promising for quantum computing, but it is unclear if they can exhibit genuine quantum behavior despite their macroscopic size.
method: The authors likely employ quantum information measures such as entanglement witnesses or quantum coherence to detect nonclassicality in molecular nanomagnets.
result: They reveal that these systems can exhibit nonclassical features under appropriate conditions, supporting their use in quantum technologies.
conclusion: Molecular nanomagnets are viable platforms for quantum information processing, and the methods used can be extended to similar systems.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm for accurate preparation of many-body quantum thermal states on near-term quantum processors by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.
motivation: Preparing thermal (Gibbs) states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and simulation, but is challenging on near-term hardware.
method: The algorithm uses periodic bath resetting and modulated coupling to efficiently drive a quantum system to its thermal state.
result: The method achieves accurate thermal state preparation on near-term quantum processors, as demonstrated experimentally or theoretically.
conclusion: Provides a practical approach for simulating finite-temperature quantum systems on current devices.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of coherent quantum routers for bucket-brigade quantum random access memory on a superconducting processor.
motivation: To realize resilient routing for quantum memories, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: They implement coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to route quantum information for bucket-brigade QRAM.
result: The demonstration achieves resilient routing for quantum memories, showcasing the functionality of quantum routers in a real hardware platform.
conclusion: The feasibility of coherent quantum routers for QRAM on superconducting processors is established, advancing quantum memory architectures.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an analytical pulse-shaping framework that extends DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, achieving single-qubit gate fidelities exceeding 99.99%.
motivation: Improving qubit gate fidelity is crucial for quantum error correction. Strong driving enables ultrafast gates but introduces multiphoton leakage, a major error source. An analytical framework to mitigate this is needed.
method: The authors extend DRAG protocols with analytical pulse shaping to specifically target and suppress multiphoton leakage pathways in strongly driven transmons.
result: The method enables ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%, as demonstrated on present superconducting hardware.
conclusion: The work provides a practical blueprint for achieving ultrahigh-fidelity gates on existing superconducting quantum processors, advancing toward fault-tolerant operation.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip semi-device-independent quantum random number generator exploiting contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: Practical quantum random number generators often rely on trusted devices, but semi-device-independent protocols offer security with fewer assumptions. Contextuality provides a resource for certified randomness with minimal device characterization, which is highly relevant for robust QRNG implementations.
method: The authors design and implement a silicon photonic chip that realizes a contextuality-based protocol for semi-device-independent randomness generation, exploiting the structure of contextuality to certify the randomness output.
result: The on-chip implementation successfully generates certified random numbers with security guarantees that rely on minimal assumptions about the internal workings of the device, demonstrating a practical step towards compact and secure QRNGs.
conclusion: The work validates contextuality as a practical resource for semi-device-independent randomness certification on an integrated photonic platform, advancing the feasibility of secure on-chip QRNGs for real-world applications.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol to prepare high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reliable entanglement between distant nodes, but existing methods for generating logical Bell pairs are resource-intensive and often demand complex connectivity.
method: The protocol employs an entanglement boosting technique that converts noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs, leveraging error correction and distillation to reduce overhead.
result: It achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pairs with significantly reduced spacetime cost and only requires 2D local connectivity, making it practical for near-term quantum hardware.
conclusion: This approach could enhance scalability of distributed quantum computing by lowering the resource overhead for entanglement generation, thus advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: 提出一种折叠横向表面码培养策略，在非局部连接架构下实现低时空开销的魔态制备。
motivation: 降低可容错量子计算中魔态制备的时空开销，特别是针对非局部连接架构。
method: 利用折叠横向门（fold-transversal gates）在表面码上进行魔态培养，优化资源消耗。
result: 与传统方法相比，显著降低了时空开销，提升了效率。
conclusion: 该策略为非局部连接架构提供了高效且实用的魔态制备途径，推进了容错量子计算的发展。

title: Asymmetric Polaron Picture For The Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Feng Qiao, Qiu-Yi Chen, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Qiao, Qiu-Yi Chen, and Zu-Jian Ying

The experimental access to ultrastrong couplings in light-matter interactions has made the quantum phase transition (QPT) in the quantum Rabi model practically relevant, while the physics of the QPT has not yet been fully explored. The polaron picture is a method capable of analyzing in the entire c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022457] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an asymmetric polaron picture to analyze the quantum phase transition in the quantum Rabi model across the entire coupling regime.
motivation: The quantum phase transition (QPT) in the quantum Rabi model has become practically relevant due to experimental access to ultrastrong couplings, yet its physics remains underexplored.
method: The authors introduce an asymmetric polaron transformation to analyze the model, providing a unified approach that captures both weak and strong coupling regimes.
result: The method yields a comprehensive understanding of the QPT, including critical behavior and the role of the asymmetry in the polaron picture.
conclusion: The polaron picture offers a new theoretical framework for the quantum Rabi model, with implications for understanding light-matter interactions in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Otto Cycle In The Anderson Impurity Model
authors: Salvatore Gatto, Alessandra Colla, Heinz-Peter Breuer, And Michael Thoss
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Gatto, Alessandra Colla, Heinz-Peter Breuer, and Michael Thoss

We study the thermodynamic performance of a periodic quantum Otto cycle operating on the single-impurity Anderson model. Using a decomposition of the time-evolution generator based on the principle of minimal dissipation, combined with the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method, w…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033233] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the thermodynamic performance of a quantum Otto cycle in the single-impurity Anderson model using minimal dissipation decomposition and hierarchical equations of motion.
motivation: To understand how many-body interactions and correlations affect the efficiency and power of quantum heat engines, using the Anderson impurity model as a working medium.
method: The authors employ a decomposition of the time-evolution generator based on the principle of minimal dissipation, combined with the numerically exact hierarchical equations of motion method to simulate the cycle.
result: The study reveals insights into the performance characteristics of the quantum Otto cycle, likely showing how interaction strength and model parameters influence efficiency and power.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate the impact of correlations on quantum thermodynamic cycles, providing a detailed case study for quantum heat engines and contributing to the design of such devices.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a self-configuring quantum network protocol that uses superposition of trajectories and variational optimization to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections.
motivation: Quantum networks suffer from decoherence and require prior knowledge of noise for configuration; the authors aim to overcome this by making the network self-configuring.
method: The protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques, allowing the network to adapt without explicit noise models.
result: The method establishes high-fidelity connections even without prior noise knowledge, demonstrating improved resilience against decoherence.
conclusion: Self-configuring quantum networks using trajectory superpositions provide a robust and practical approach for quantum communication, advancing network architecture and protocol design.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact parabolic mirror on an optical chip enables efficient photon extraction from neutral atoms, advancing practical quantum network nodes.
motivation: Quantum networking with neutral atoms requires highly efficient and stable photon collection; existing approaches are bulky or inefficient.
method: The authors fabricated an optical chip with a parabolic mirror that focuses atomic emission into an optical fiber, achieving a compact, mechanically stable design with high collection efficiency.
result: The device demonstrates efficient photon extraction suitable for quantum networking experiments, with performance comparable to or better than larger macroscopic setups.
conclusion: This chip-scale parabolic mirror provides a practical and scalable component for building future quantum network nodes with neutral atoms.

title: Symmetry Enforcing Entanglement At High Temperatures
authors: Amir-Reza Negari, Leonardo A. Lessa, And Subhayan Sahu
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari, Leonardo A. Lessa, and Subhayan Sahu

Many-body quantum systems with local interactions undergo “sudden death of entanglement” at high temperatures, whereby thermal states become classical mixtures of product states. We investigate whether symmetry constraints can prevent this phenomenon. We prove that strongly symmetric thermal states …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022458] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that symmetry constraints can prevent the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature thermal states of many-body quantum systems.
motivation: High-temperature thermal states typically lose quantum entanglement, which is crucial for quantum information tasks; understanding mechanisms that preserve entanglement is of fundamental importance.
method: The authors analyze strongly symmetric thermal states of local Hamiltonians and use rigorous mathematical proofs to demonstrate that entanglement is maintained at high temperatures.
result: They show that strong symmetry ensures the presence of entanglement even at high temperatures, counteracting the usual sudden death of entanglement.
conclusion: Symmetry provides a protective mechanism for entanglement in thermal many-body systems, potentially enabling quantum applications at elevated temperatures.

title: Probability-current Reorganization Lowers The Cost Of Finite-time Brownian Erasure
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Finite-time information erasure is governed by probability transport through configuration space, not only by final logical populations. We show that a two-dimensional Brownian memory can lower fast-erasure cost by reorganizing probability currents through a transverse degree of freedom. Using physi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022108] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that a two-dimensional Brownian memory can lower the thermodynamic cost of fast erasure by reorganizing probability currents through a transverse degree of freedom.
motivation: Finite-time information erasure cost is not only determined by final logical populations but also by probability transport, motivating a search for strategies to reduce the cost.
method: The authors analyze a two-dimensional Brownian memory and demonstrate that reorganizing probability currents via a transverse degree of freedom can lower the erasure cost.
result: They quantitatively show that such reorganization reduces the thermodynamic cost compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: The findings provide a new mechanism to optimize finite-time information erasure, relevant to thermodynamic efficiency of information processing.

title: Global Topological Protection Of Entanglement In Integrated Photonic Quantum Walks
authors: Liat Nemirovsky-Levy, Yonatan Plotnik, Alexander Palatnik, Mark Lyubarov, Ohad Segal, Yaron Oz, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Liat Nemirovsky-Levy, Yonatan Plotnik, Alexander Palatnik, Mark Lyubarov, Ohad Segal, Yaron Oz, and Mordechai Segev

Photon entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum technologies, yet it is extremely fragile especially in large quantum circuitry, which is necessary for quantum information processing and computing. We propose an integrated scheme for direct topological protection of entanglement, enabling …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033215] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an integrated photonic scheme to directly protect photon entanglement via topological effects in quantum walks.
motivation: Photon entanglement is fragile in large quantum circuits, which is a barrier to scalable quantum information processing.
method: The paper designs an integrated photonic quantum walk architecture that leverages topological protection to preserve entanglement.
result: The scheme enables global topological protection of entanglement, making it robust against noise and disorder.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to protect entanglement in integrated photonic devices, advancing quantum information technology.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations as a computational method to bound quantum correlations in quantum information problems.
motivation: Computing quantum correlations is crucial yet challenging, requiring efficient numerical methods to characterize the set of quantum correlations.
method: The authors develop semidefinite programming relaxations using block-matrix structures to approximate and bound quantum correlations.
result: The method provides tight bounds and is applicable to a wide range of quantum information tasks, demonstrating its versatility.
conclusion: This computational approach advances the study of quantum correlations and offers a practical tool for quantum information research.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Spontaneous spin ordering makes superradiance robust against disorder in waveguide QED systems.
motivation: Superradiance is often degraded by disorder in emitter frequencies and positions; this paper investigates whether self-organization can overcome this.
method: Theoretical analysis of a many-body spin chain coupled to a waveguide, accounting for spatial and spectral disorder.
result: They find that the system spontaneously orders spins to maintain coherent emission, protecting superradiance against strong disorder.
conclusion: This robustness could enable robust quantum light sources and quantum network applications.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: Noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, impacting the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement is a key resource in quantum circuits, and understanding its robustness to noise is essential for both foundational physics and practical quantum computing.
method: The study likely analyzes 2D random circuits with measurements and noise, using theoretical or numerical approaches to determine how entanglement is affected.
result: It is shown that noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement, which has implications for the classical simulation of noisy quantum devices.
conclusion: The findings highlight the fragility of quantum advantages in the presence of noise, constraining the regimes where quantum computation offers a benefit.

title: Heitler Effect And Resonance Fluorescence In Quantum Magnonics
authors: Enes Ilbuğa, V. V. Dobrovitski, And Ya. M. Blanter
abstract:
Author(s): Enes Ilbuğa, V. V. Dobrovitski, and Ya. M. Blanter

We consider a coupled system of a qubit and a magnon mode in which the qubit is weakly driven. We demonstrate that the spectral steady-state responses of both the qubit and the magnon show, in addition to two sidebands split by the coupling, also a peak at the driving frequency with virtually zero l…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074434] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of a driven qubit-magnon system showing a Heitler peak in the spectral response.
motivation: To understand the spectral properties of a coupled qubit-magnon system under weak driving, relevant for quantum magnonics and hybrid quantum devices.
method: Quantum optics description of the coupled system, solving for steady-state spectra.
result: Both qubit and magnon spectra exhibit sidebands split by the coupling and an additional peak at the driving frequency with virtually zero linewidth (Heitler effect).
conclusion: The Heitler effect manifests in quantum magnonics, providing new insights into the dynamics of hybrid systems.

title: Predicting Entanglement Entropy From Particle Tunneling Of Interacting Fermions Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
authors: Elvira Bilokon, Valeriia Bilokon, Abhijit Sen, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Andrii G. Sotnikov, And Denys I. Bondar
abstract:
Author(s): Elvira Bilokon, Valeriia Bilokon, Abhijit Sen, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Andrii G. Sotnikov, and Denys I. Bondar

Entanglement entropy is a fundamental measure of quantum correlations and a key resource underpinning advances in quantum information and many-body physics. We uncover a universal relationship between bipartite entanglement entropy and particle number after the barrier in a one-dimensional Fermi-Hub…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033243] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to uncover a universal relationship between bipartite entanglement entropy and particle number after a barrier in a one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a fundamental measure of quantum correlations, and understanding its dependence on particle tunneling could provide new insights into many-body quantum systems.
method: The authors train Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks on data from the Fermi-Hubbard model to predict entanglement entropy from the particle number after a barrier.
result: They discover a universal relationship that allows accurate prediction of entanglement entropy from simple particle counts, validated across different system parameters.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that machine learning can reveal and exploit universal connections between particle transport and entanglement, offering a new predictive tool for many-body physics.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a holographic duality mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order, providing a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: To better understand and classify quantum phases in open systems, particularly addressing limitations of existing frameworks in describing mixed-state symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: By establishing a duality between boundary mixed states and bulk topological order, the authors develop a theoretical mapping that relates properties of open quantum systems to those of higher-dimensional topological phases.
result: The framework successfully characterizes strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases, offering new insights into the structure of mixed-state order.
conclusion: This holographic duality provides a novel and powerful tool for studying quantum many-body systems, with potential implications for quantum information and condensed matter physics.

title: Directional Information Transfer Between Interacting Brownian Particles
authors: Tenta Tani
abstract:
Author(s): Tenta Tani

We theoretically investigate how information flows when two particles interact with each other. Understanding the physical mechanisms of directional information flow is crucial for advancing information thermodynamics and stochastic computing. However, the fundamental connection between mechanical m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024147] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates how directional information flows between interacting Brownian particles, connecting mechanical motion to information thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding physical mechanisms of directional information flow is crucial for advancing information thermodynamics and stochastic computing.
method: The theoretical approach likely combines stochastic thermodynamics with information-theoretic measures to analyze two interacting particles.
result: The study reveals fundamental connections between mechanical interactions and the direction of information transfer.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physical basis of information flow in stochastic systems, relevant to thermodynamics and computation.

title: Statistical-gauge Covariance In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Statistical-gauge structures generated by current operators provide a symmetry-based description of forces and hyperforces in closed quantum statistical mechanics, but their status in open quantum dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we develop a generalized statistical-gauge framework for Mark…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024141] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized statistical-gauge framework for Markovian open quantum systems, extending symmetry-based descriptions of forces from closed to open dynamics.
motivation: To understand and describe forces and hyperforces in open quantum systems using a symmetry-based statistical-gauge approach, which was previously only developed for closed systems.
method: The author constructs a generalized statistical-gauge framework tailored to Markovian open quantum dynamics, incorporating current operators and gauge covariance.
result: The framework successfully provides a symmetry-based description of forces in open quantum systems, demonstrating gauge covariance and extending the closed-system formalism.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap by applying statistical-gauge methods to open quantum systems, offering a new theoretical tool for analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Regularized Counterdiabatic Driving For The Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Pablo García-Azorín, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Xi Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Julián Ferreiro-Vélez, Pablo García-Azorín, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Xi Chen

Counterdiabatic (CD) driving provides a powerful route to fast and robust state preparation by suppressing diabatic excitations during finite-time evolution. Yet, deriving analytical CD protocols for complex systems remains challenging, motivating the development of variational approaches. These met…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033244] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a regularized counterdiabatic driving protocol for the quantum Rabi model, enabling fast and robust state preparation by suppressing diabatic excitations.
motivation: Analytical counterdiabatic protocols are difficult to derive for complex quantum systems, prompting variational approaches, but these often lack accuracy or efficiency. A regularized method is proposed to improve state preparation performance.
method: The authors introduce a regularization technique to the variational counterdiabatic driving framework and apply it to the quantum Rabi model, deriving a systematic protocol that minimizes diabatic errors.
result: The regularized CD protocol achieves high-fidelity state preparation with significantly reduced time compared to adiabatic evolution, demonstrated via numerical simulations for the quantum Rabi model.
conclusion: The regularized approach provides a practical improvement for quantum control in hybrid quantum systems, offering potential benefits for quantum information processing and thermodynamic operations.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: 该论文提出一个从实验数据学习哈密顿量和Lindblad算子并给出有界误差的框架，用于验证大规模量子模拟。
motivation: 大规模量子模拟需要验证其准确性，但直接验证成本高，需要从数据中推断动力学并给出误差界限。
method: 通过哈密顿量学习和Lindblad学习，基于测量数据推断系统参数，并利用优化和统计方法给出误差界限。
result: 在实验环境中验证了该框架，能够准确推断动力学并提供误差界限。
conclusion: 该框架为量子模拟验证提供了一种可扩展的方法，有助于构建可靠的量子模拟器。

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor completely determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states in the resource theory of asymmetry for any compact Lie group.
motivation: Understanding conversion rates in resource theories is fundamental; prior results were limited to specific groups or dimensionalities, and a general characterization was missing.
method: The authors formulate the conversion problem in the resource theory of asymmetry and derive a rate expression in terms of the quantum geometric tensor, leveraging group representation theory and smooth manifolds.
result: They show that the pure-state i.i.d. conversion rate is exactly given by the ratio of the quantum geometric tensors of the source and target states, for any compact Lie group.
conclusion: This provides a complete and elegant result for conversion rates in asymmetry resource theories, with implications for quantum metrology, thermodynamics, and quantum information processing.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez
abstract:
Author(s): Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, and Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates creation of defect-free neutral-atom arrays at the thousand-atom scale in a cryogenic environment, enabling long-lived single-atom trapping for quantum computing.
motivation: To scale neutral-atom quantum computing, it is necessary to create large defect-free arrays with long coherence times; cryogenic operation reduces decoherence and improves stability.
method: Utilizes a cryogenic environment with high optical access to trap and assemble neutral atoms into perfect arrays using optical tweezers.
result: Achieves defect-free arrays containing thousands of atoms, with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds.
conclusion: This work represents a key milestone towards large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing, enabling more complex quantum information processing.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, enabling new fault-tolerant quantum computation platforms.
motivation: To extend quantum error correction to exotic topological orders, which may offer advantages for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: Constructs novel chiral color codes—three-dimensional stabilizer codes—designed to support single-shot error correction.
result: Achieves single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating a new class of fault-tolerant codes.
conclusion: These codes provide promising new platforms for practical fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a scheme to accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation using good quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, achieving constant qubit overhead and low time overhead via parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically suffers from high qubit and time overhead, limiting practical scalability. The authors aim to reduce these overheads by leveraging good quantum LDPC codes and advanced techniques.
method: The authors propose a framework that combines good quantum LDPC codes with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation, enabling efficient fault-tolerant operations with constant qubit overhead.
result: Their scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving the resource efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can substantially accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more feasible for near-term and future quantum processors.

title: Permutation-invariant Holstein-Primakoff Spin Codes For Local And Collective Noise
authors: Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, Tyler G. Thurtell, Andrew K. Forbes, Vikas Buchemmavari, And Ben Q. Baragiola
abstract:
Author(s): Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, Tyler G. Thurtell, Andrew K. Forbes, Vikas Buchemmavari, and Ben Q. Baragiola

Quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation, yet most existing codes rely on local control and stabilizer measurements that are difficult to implement in systems dominated by collective interactions. Inspired by S. Omanakuttan and T. J. Volkoff, Spin-squeezed Gottesm…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022467] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces permutation-invariant Holstein-Primakoff spin codes designed to be robust against both local and collective noise, offering a new class of quantum error correction codes for systems with collective interactions.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction codes often require local control and stabilizer measurements that are impractical in systems dominated by collective interactions, necessitating codes tailored to such environments.
method: The authors construct permutation-invariant codes based on the Holstein-Primakoff representation, generalizing spin-squeezed Gottesman codes to handle both local and collective noise.
result: The proposed codes provide robust error correction against collective noise while maintaining compatibility with local noise models, potentially enhancing fault-tolerance in collective-interaction systems.
conclusion: These permutation-invariant codes offer a promising approach to quantum error correction in platforms where collective noise is prevalent, expanding the toolbox for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Tunable Quantum Mpemba Effect In Long-range Interacting Systems
authors: Andrew Hallam, Matthew Yusuf, Aashish A. Clerk, Ivar Martin, And Zlatko Papić
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew Hallam, Matthew Yusuf, Aashish A. Clerk, Ivar Martin, and Zlatko Papić

Symmetry plays a fundamental role in many-body systems, both in and out of equilibrium. The quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—a phenomenon where systems initially farther from equilibrium can thermalize faster—can be understood in terms of how rapidly a symmetry, broken by initial conditions, is dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125135] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a tunable quantum Mpemba effect in long-range interacting systems, where initial states farther from equilibrium can thermalize faster due to symmetry dynamics.
motivation: Understanding anomalous thermalization phenomena like the Mpemba effect in quantum many-body systems, and how symmetry breaking and long-range interactions influence relaxation.
method: The authors analyze symmetry dynamics and thermalization in long-range interacting models, likely using numerical simulations or analytical arguments to demonstrate tunable conditions for the quantum Mpemba effect.
result: They show that the quantum Mpemba effect can be tuned by controlling parameters such as interaction range or initial conditions, and relate the effect to the rate of symmetry restoration.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and thermalization, offering a controllable framework for observing the Mpemba effect in many-body systems.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis to thermal first-order phase transitions, revealing coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: To understand how eigenstate thermalization behaves in systems undergoing thermal first-order phase transitions, where standard ETH assumptions may break down.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis, likely combining perturbative and numerical approaches, to study eigenstate properties across the transition.
result: They demonstrate that first-order transitions require a generalized ETH with multiple eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like superposition states.
conclusion: The work extends the framework of ETH to encompass first-order phase transitions, providing new insights into quantum thermalization in discontinuous transitions.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature entanglement properties, despite being at zero energy.
motivation: To explore whether local Hamiltonians can have eigenstates (including the ground state) that mimic infinite-temperature thermal states, which is relevant to eigenstate thermalization and quantum many-body physics.
method: The authors provide an explicit construction of local Hamiltonians with carefully chosen interactions to ensure the ground state has extensive entanglement characteristic of infinite-temperature states.
result: They demonstrate that it is possible to have zero-energy ground states with extensive entanglement, defying the typical low-entanglement expectation for ground states.
conclusion: The findings have implications for the understanding of thermalization and entanglement in quantum systems, suggesting local Hamiltonians can host highly entangled states at zero energy.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to errors.
method: The authors propose a polynomial-time algorithm to design such gates, likely using numerical optimization or systematic pulse shaping.
result: The method achieves gate design across hundreds of qubits, demonstrating scalability.
conclusion: This work offers a scalable route to large-scale trapped-ion quantum computers.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
