Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion, the triangle criterion, for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed quantum states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a simple and operational criterion for magic in mixed states, which is important for quantum computing but challenging to characterize.
method: By drawing inspiration from entanglement theory, they propose a criterion based on certain conditions that identify nonstabilizerness.
result: The criterion allows detection of nonstabilizerness and certification of undistillability, applicable to mixed states.
conclusion: This work advances the resource theory of magic by providing a computable criterion, with implications for magic distillation and detection.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by Rydberg atom decay due to blackbody radiation; extending Rydberg lifetimes is critical for improving gate performance.
method: The authors operate an optical tweezer array in a cryogenic environment to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, then measure Rydberg lifetimes and characterize the improvement.
result: They observe substantially extended Rydberg lifetimes, which mitigates relaxation errors and enhances the feasibility of high-fidelity two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation effectively improves Rydberg qubit coherence, directly benefiting the scalability and reliability of neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical analysis of a nonlinear cosφ coupling that suppresses measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits, aimed at enabling higher-fidelity readout.
motivation: Improving transmon qubit readout fidelity is critical, and measurement-induced state transitions during readout are a known obstacle.
method: The authors perform experiments and numerical simulations on transmon qubits with a cosφ coupling, analyzing the dynamics of the nonlinear interaction to understand its effect on state transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to enhanced readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ coupling mechanism offers a promising approach for improving transmon readout performance.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces twisted color circuits, a family of fault-tolerant circuits for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, using a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To achieve scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with non-Clifford gates on a 2D color code device with limited connectivity.
method: The authors design a family of circuits, called twisted color circuits, and demonstrate how they can be implemented on a planar chip with nearest-neighbor couplings, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance, enabling universal quantum computing with non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
conclusion: This work advances fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a practical circuit construction for non-Clifford gates on a planar architecture.

title: Enhanced Quantum Metrology By Criticality-Assisted Noncommutative Preparation
authors: Ningxin Kong, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Qiongyi He
abstract:
Author(s): Ningxin Kong, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Qiongyi He

Quantum criticality is a resource for quantum-enhanced metrology, but existing schemes face intrinsic limitations. These arise because using criticality directly in the encoding dynamics restricts the accessible parameters to those explicitly supported by the critical Hamiltonian, and the requiremen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090801] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new quantum metrology scheme using criticality and noncommutative preparation to overcome limitations of direct criticality encoding, enhancing precision.
motivation: Existing quantum metrology using criticality restricts accessible parameters and has other limitations; the authors aim to circumvent these by decoupling preparation from encoding.
method: The method involves preparing the probe state in a noncommutative way relative to the critical Hamiltonian, enabling sensitivity to parameters not directly supported by the Hamiltonian.
result: The scheme achieves enhanced metrological performance, likely in terms of quantum Fisher information or precision bounds.
conclusion: The proposed approach broadens the applicability of criticality-based metrology and demonstrates a new resource for quantum-enhanced measurements.

title: Fisher Information Of Complete Quantum Measurements
authors: Rakesh Saini, Jukka Kiukas, Daniel Burgarth, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Rakesh Saini, Jukka Kiukas, Daniel Burgarth, and Alexei Gilchrist

Informationally complete measurements form the foundation of universal quantum state reconstruction, while quantum parameter estimation is based on the local structure of the manifold of quantum states. In this work, we establish a link between these two aspects within the context of a single inform…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022465] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper links informationally complete measurements to quantum parameter estimation via Fisher information, unifying these two aspects of quantum state characterization.
motivation: Informationally complete measurements enable universal quantum state reconstruction, while parameter estimation relies on the local geometry of the state manifold; the work aims to bridge these perspectives.
method: The authors analyze the Fisher information of complete quantum measurements, deriving properties that connect the global information content of such measurements to local estimation precision.
result: A formal relationship is established between the Fisher information of informationally complete measurements and the parameters being estimated, providing insight into the efficiency of quantum state tomography.
conclusion: The findings offer a unified framework for understanding quantum measurements in both state reconstruction and metrological tasks, potentially guiding optimal measurement design.

title: Impact Of Acoustic Phonons On Biexciton Preparation Using Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Sutirtha Biswas, Dionisis Stefanatos, And Emmanuel Paspalakis
abstract:
Author(s): Sutirtha Biswas, Dionisis Stefanatos, and Emmanuel Paspalakis

We investigate the impact of acoustic phonons on biexciton preparation in an InGaAs/GaAs semiconductor quantum dot driven by laser pulses designed using shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA). The electronic dynamics is calculated with the time-evolving matrix product operator (TEMPO) algorithm, which prov…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022622] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how acoustic phonons affect the fidelity of biexciton preparation in InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots when using shortcuts to adiabaticity, using the TEMPO algorithm to model the dynamics.
motivation: To understand the impact of phonon-induced decoherence on quantum control protocols in quantum dots, which is crucial for implementing high-fidelity quantum gates.
method: Uses the time-evolving matrix product operator (TEMPO) algorithm to compute the electronic dynamics exactly, accounting for the interaction with acoustic phonons, and compares STA-driven pulses with conventional approaches.
result: Finds that phonons degrade the fidelity of biexciton preparation, but STA pulses can mitigate some effects depending on pulse duration and detuning.
conclusion: Provides guidance on optimizing pulse parameters to minimize phonon effects, improving the viability of STA for quantum dot-based quantum information processing.

title: Timing Quantum Emission: Coherence, Superradiance, And Entanglement In Order
authors: Nur Fadhillah Binti Rahimi, Norman Tze Wei Koo, Daniel Schumayer, Christopher Gies, Leong Chuan Kwek, And David A. W. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): Nur Fadhillah Binti Rahimi, Norman Tze Wei Koo, Daniel Schumayer, Christopher Gies, Leong Chuan Kwek, and David A. W. Hutchinson

We investigate the short-term temporal dynamics of superradiance in closely spaced quantum emitters. Building on Dicke's 1954 framework, we analyze the sequential emergence of coherence, superradiance, and entanglement, revealing a distinct temporal hierarchy in their extremal values: relative coher…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023728] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the temporal hierarchy of coherence, superradiance, and entanglement in closely spaced quantum emitters, revealing a distinct sequential ordering in their extremal values.
motivation: Understanding the short-term dynamics of superradiance is fundamental to quantum optics and may inform quantum information protocols. The study builds on Dicke's framework to explore the interplay between coherence and entanglement.
method: The authors analyze the temporal dynamics of quantum emitters using the Dicke model, examining the sequential emergence of coherence, superradiance, and entanglement through theoretical derivations.
result: They find a distinct temporal hierarchy: relative coherence peaks first, followed by superradiance, and then entanglement, indicating a systematic ordering in their extremal values.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the relationship between coherence and collective emission, potentially useful for quantum information processing where timing and entanglement control are important.

title: Quantum Observables Over Time For Information Recovery
authors: Gabriele Bressanini, Farhan Hanif, Hyukjoon Kwon, And M. S. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriele Bressanini, Farhan Hanif, Hyukjoon Kwon, and M. S. Kim

We introduce the concept of quantum observables over time (QOOT), an operator that jointly describes two observables at two distinct time points, as a dual of the quantum state over time formalism. We provide a full characterization of the conditions under which a QOOT can be properly defined, via a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033208] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Introduces quantum observables over time (QOOT) as a dual of the quantum state over time formalism, providing a full characterization of when such operators can be defined.
motivation: To jointly describe observables at two distinct time points and enable information recovery across time in quantum systems.
method: Formal definition of QOOT operators and derivation of conditions for their existence, likely using operator algebra and quantum measurement theory.
result: Provides a complete set of conditions under which QOOT can be properly defined, potentially enabling new insights into time-dependent quantum information.
conclusion: Establishes a novel framework for time-dependent quantum observables, with implications for quantum information recovery and foundations.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes out-of-time-order correlation functions in a minimal quantum circuit model using free probability, establishing a mapping between system-bath interactions and free probability structures.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and thermalization in simple circuit models, and to explore the applicability of free probability in characterizing OTOCs.
method: The authors analyze a minimal quantum circuit model and map system-bath interactions to free probability structures to compute OTOCs analytically.
result: They derive new results for OTOCs in the circuit model, revealing universal behavior linked to free probability and providing insights into quantum chaos.
conclusion: Free probability provides a powerful framework for analyzing OTOCs in quantum circuits, deepening our understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves no-go theorems showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limitations of fault-tolerant quantum computing, specifically whether standard gadgets can realize all necessary logical gates.
method: The authors analyze common classes of fault-tolerant constructions and prove impossibility results using group-theoretic and coding-theoretic arguments.
result: They demonstrate that these constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group, imposing fundamental constraints on fault-tolerant schemes.
conclusion: The no-go theorem highlights inherent limitations in current fault-tolerance approaches and may guide the design of alternative schemes.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: To achieve scalable quantum computation with a novel qubit platform that is robust and highly tunable.
method: Designs an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, likely involving theoretical modeling and analysis of qubit properties.
result: Identifies a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation through the proposed architecture, demonstrating feasibility and tunability.
conclusion: The architecture shows promise for robust and scalable electron qubits, contributing to hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.
motivation: Fast and high-fidelity qubit readout is essential for quantum computing, but standard readout methods suffer from Purcell decay that limits coherence times.
method: The authors introduce a nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling scheme that provides intrinsic Purcell protection, enabling faster readout without compromising qubit coherence.
result: The approach demonstrates high-fidelity, fast readout while preserving qubit coherence, promising significant improvements for superconducting quantum processors.
conclusion: This readout technique offers a practical solution for scalable quantum computation with enhanced measurement performance and coherence protection.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the advantages of using metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.
motivation: To explore a new physical platform exploiting the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced quantum control and simulation capabilities.
method: The authors create arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezers and analyze their properties for quantum simulation with tunable hopping and for continuous-variable quantum computing.
result: They show that the small mass of helium-3 enables significant advantages for quantum simulation of materials and continuous-variable quantum computing.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 atom arrays are a promising platform for advancing quantum science.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes that balances high decoding accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction demands fast and accurate decoders, but existing methods often suffer from high computational overhead or latency, hindering practical implementation.
method: The authors adapt the beam search algorithm to the structure of quantum LDPC codes, allowing parallel exploration of multiple error hypotheses to efficiently identify the most likely correction.
result: The proposed decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency constraints, and reduces the requirement for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder provides a practical and efficient solution for real-time quantum error correction with LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.
motivation: To understand the behavior of noisy random quantum circuits, specifically the onset of anticoncentration, which is crucial for quantum advantage and classical simulability.
method: The paper likely uses analytical techniques, possibly statistical mechanics mappings or tensor networks, to analyze the output distributions of random circuits under noise.
result: It finds universal depth-dependent regimes and shows that anticoncentration is independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework to describe noisy random circuits, with implications for quantum computing and complexity.

title: Refined Coherent Control Of Atomic Qubits Via A Wave-function Approach Conditioned On No-decay
authors: Yuan Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan Sun

As a fundamental phenomenon in quantum systems, spontaneous emission constitutes an inevitable source of error, which ultimately degrades the fidelity of quantum logic gates. A successful quantum logic gate needs to operate on the condition that no decay event, such as spontaneous emission, occurs. …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022621] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a refined wave-function approach conditioned on no-decay to improve coherent control of atomic qubits affected by spontaneous emission.
motivation: Spontaneous emission is a fundamental source of error that degrades quantum gate fidelity, so there is a need for control methods that operate effectively in the presence of such decay.
method: The author develops a wave-function approach that conditions the control evolution on the absence of decay events, effectively filtering out erroneous trajectories.
result: The approach is shown to improve the fidelity of quantum logic gates for atomic qubits by mitigating the impact of spontaneous emission.
conclusion: The conditioned wave-function method offers a viable path to more robust coherent control of atomic qubits, which is relevant for quantum computing platforms.

title: Complete Classification Of Integrability And Nonintegrability For Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Chain With Symmetric Nearest-neighbor Interaction
authors: Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, And Naoto Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, and Naoto Shiraishi

General spin-[MATH] chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interaction are studied. We rigorously prove that all spin models in this class, except for known integrable systems, are nonintegrable in the sense that they possess no nontrivial local conserved quantities. This result confirms that…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033240] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously classifies spin-1/2 chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interactions, proving that all but a few known integrable models lack nontrivial local conserved quantities, i.e., are nonintegrable.
motivation: Understanding integrability and its absence is crucial for characterizing thermalization and quantum chaos in many-body systems.
method: The authors employ rigorous mathematical proofs to analyze the existence of local conserved quantities for the entire class of models.
result: Complete classification: every model in this class is either integrable (belonging to known integrable systems) or nonintegrable, with no local conservation laws beyond the trivial ones.
conclusion: The result confirms that nonintegrability is generic in this family, providing a definitive foundation for studies of thermalization and quantum chaos in such spin chains.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a sliding-window estimation approach to track time-varying error rates, improving quantum error correction decoder performance.
motivation: Realistic quantum systems experience drifting noise, and static error estimates degrade decoder performance.
method: Uses sliding-window estimation to reconstruct time-varying error rates and integrates into the decoder.
result: Improved decoder performance under time-varying noise conditions.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is beneficial for practical quantum error correction.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a loss-invariant method to certify quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum light is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are sensitive to losses.
method: The authors use phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification combined with simple intensity detection to certify quantum non-Gaussianity in a loss-invariant way, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.
result: The method provides a robust certification of non-classicality and non-Gaussianity even in the presence of losses, as shown experimentally.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and loss-tolerant tool for characterizing quantum resources in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators to improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity, providing a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: High-coherence mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are crucial for quantum information processing, but losses limit their performance.
method: The authors systematically characterize loss mechanisms and optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in multimode bulk acoustic resonators, likely through experimental fabrication and measurement.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence time and cooperativity by identifying optimal transducer materials and designs.
conclusion: The findings provide a practical materials blueprint for advancing quantum acoustic devices integrated with superconducting circuits.

title: Elucidating The Intersystem Crossing Of The Nitrogen-Vacancy Center Up To Megabar Pressures
authors: Benchen Huang, Srinivas V. Mandyam, Weijie Wu, Bryce Kobrin, Prabudhya Bhattacharyya, Yu Jin, Bijuan Chen, Max Block, Esther Wang, Zhipan Wang, Satcher Hsieh, Chong Zu, Christopher R. Laumann, Norman Y. Yao, And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Benchen Huang, Srinivas V. Mandyam, Weijie Wu, Bryce Kobrin, Prabudhya Bhattacharyya, Yu Jin, Bijuan Chen, Max Block, Esther Wang, Zhipan Wang, Satcher Hsieh, Chong Zu, Christopher R. Laumann, Norman Y. Yao, and Giulia Galli

The integration of nitrogen-vacancy color centers into diamond anvil cells has opened the door to quantum sensing at megabar pressures. Despite a multitude of experimental demonstrations and applications ranging from quantum materials to geophysics, a detailed microscopic understanding of how stress…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 093801] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a microscopic understanding of the intersystem crossing of nitrogen-vacancy centers under megabar pressures, addressing a critical gap for quantum sensing applications.
motivation: NV centers integrated into diamond anvil cells enable quantum sensing at extreme pressures, but the effect of stress on their intersystem crossing is not well understood.
method: The study likely combines theoretical modeling (e.g., first-principles calculations) with experimental measurements to analyze the intersystem crossing rate under high pressure.
result: The paper reveals how pressure modifies the intersystem crossing, impacting the spin and optical properties of NV centers.
conclusion: The findings enhance our understanding of NV centers under extreme conditions, which is crucial for developing robust quantum sensors and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Time Correlations From Steady-State Expectation Values
authors: Wojciech Górecki, Simone Felicetti, Lorenzo Maccone, And Roberto Di Candia
abstract:
Author(s): Wojciech Górecki, Simone Felicetti, Lorenzo Maccone, and Roberto Di Candia

Recovering properties of correlation functions is typically challenging. On the one hand, experimentally, it requires measurements with a temporal resolution finer than the system’s dynamics. On the other hand, analytical or numerical analysis requires solving the system evolution. Here, we use rece…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090401] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to reconstruct time correlation functions from steady-state expectation values, enabling the study of dynamics without fast time-resolved measurements.
motivation: Directly measuring time correlations requires high temporal resolution or solving the system evolution, which is often impractical; the authors aim to circumvent this by extracting correlation information from steady-state data.
method: The authors propose using a receiver (or measurement scheme) that couples to the system in a way that the steady-state expectation values contain information about the two-time correlation functions, allowing reconstruction via suitable processing.
result: They demonstrate that time correlations can be recovered from steady-state measurements, potentially simplifying experimental and theoretical analysis of quantum dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for studying time-dependent properties in quantum systems without requiring ultrafast measurement capabilities.

title: Correlated Decoherence In A Common Environment Activated By Relative Motion
authors: Yang Wang, Zhilei Sun, Feiyi Liu, Min Guo, Yuhan Jiang, And Mingyang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Wang, Zhilei Sun, Feiyi Liu, Min Guo, Yuhan Jiang, and Mingyang Liu

We study two spatially separated boundary subsystems coupled to a common structured environment under relative motion within a Gaussian open-system framework. By integrating out the environment, we obtain an influence functional governed by a dressed environmental correlator evaluated at the boundar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022218] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: 本研究在相对运动条件下，通过高斯开放系统框架分析了两个空间分离边界子系统在共同环境中的关联退相干。
motivation: 理解相对运动对开放量子系统中退相干和量子关联的影响，为量子信息处理中的复杂环境效应提供理论基础。
method: 采用高斯开放系统框架，积分掉环境得到影响泛函，该泛函由边界处的dressed环境相关函数控制。
result: 揭示了相对运动如何通过修改环境相关函数影响两个子系统的退相干动力学和量子关联。
conclusion: 相对运动可激活共同环境中的关联退相干，对量子网络和量子信息处理中的环境控制有重要意义。

title: Boundary-induced Phases In The Dissipative Dicke Lattice Model
authors: Peng-Fei Wei, Yilun Xu, Fengxiao Sun, Qiongyi He, Peter Rabl, And Zhihai Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Peng-Fei Wei, Yilun Xu, Fengxiao Sun, Qiongyi He, Peter Rabl, and Zhihai Wang

The superradiant phase transition in the dissipative Dicke lattice model, driven by on-site collective atom-photon couplings and intersite photon hopping, is a cornerstone of nonequilibrium quantum many-body physics. However, little is still known about the influence of boundaries in experimental ac…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023731] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies boundary effects in the dissipative Dicke lattice model, revealing boundary-induced phases in a non-equilibrium quantum many-body system.
motivation: Boundaries are ubiquitous in experimental realizations of the Dicke lattice, yet their influence on the superradiant phase transition is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the dissipative Dicke lattice model with a Lindblad master equation, investigating how boundary conditions alter the steady-state phase diagram.
result: They identify distinct boundary-induced phases that differ from the bulk behavior, demonstrating that boundaries can significantly modify the phase structure.
conclusion: Boundary terms must be considered for accurate predictions and interpretations in experimental dissipative systems.

title: General Perturbation Theory For Local Quantum Uncertainty And Its Formulation In The Linear-response Regime
authors: A. A. Jimenez-Romero And F. Rojas
abstract:
Author(s): A. A. Jimenez-Romero and F. Rojas

We develop a general perturbation theory for the local quantum uncertainty (LQU), a discord-type quantifier of nonclassicality based on the Wigner-Yanase skew information. Starting from a perturbed density matrix [MATH], we derive an explicit first-order expansion of [MATH] using …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022468] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a general perturbation theory for the local quantum uncertainty, a discord-type measure, and presents its formulation in the linear-response regime.
motivation: To provide a systematic way to compute local quantum uncertainty under small perturbations, which is important for understanding quantum correlations in noisy or driven systems.
method: Starting from a perturbed density matrix, the authors derive an explicit first-order expansion of the local quantum uncertainty and express it in the linear-response regime.
result: They obtain a general expression for the first-order correction to local quantum uncertainty under arbitrary perturbations.
conclusion: This framework enables the calculation of local quantum uncertainty in various physical scenarios, potentially advancing the study of quantum discord in realistic settings.

title: Full-state Information-disturbance Tradeoff For Direction Estimation With Antiparallel Spin-coherent Pairs
authors: Massimiliano F. Sacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Massimiliano F. Sacchi

We determine the optimal information-disturbance tradeoff for estimating an unknown spatial direction encoded in two antiparallel spins. Rotational covariance reduces the optimization over all instruments to a finite-dimensional Choi problem: a positive seed operator obeys one trace constraint for e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022466] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper determines the optimal information-disturbance tradeoff for estimating a spatial direction from antiparallel spin-coherent pairs, reducing the optimization to a finite-dimensional Choi problem.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits on how much information can be extracted about a direction from quantum states without disturbing them.
method: Uses rotational covariance to simplify the optimization over all quantum instruments to a finite-dimensional Choi problem with trace constraints.
result: Provides the explicit optimal tradeoff and likely the achievable bound for such estimation tasks.
conclusion: Establishes a rigorous bound on the information-disturbance relationship for direction estimation with spin-coherent states.

title: Squeezed Quantum Multiplets: Properties And Phase Space Representation
authors: Juan Pablo Paz, Corina Révora, And Christian Tomás Schmiegelow
abstract:
Author(s): Juan Pablo Paz, Corina Révora, and Christian Tomás Schmiegelow

We define and study the properties of squeezed quantum multiplets, which are sets of [MATH]-orthonormal quantum states formed by superpositions of states squeezed along [MATH] equally spaced directions in quadrature space. We present analytical expressions for phase-space distributions (Wigner and charact…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022459] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines squeezed quantum multiplets, a set of orthonormal quantum states formed by superpositions of squeezed states along equally spaced directions, and provides analytical expressions for their Wigner and characteristic functions.
motivation: To introduce and characterize a new class of continuous-variable quantum states that may have applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct the states by superposing squeezed states along M directions and compute analytical forms for phase-space distributions.
result: They derive expressions for the Wigner and characteristic functions of these multiplet states.
conclusion: The analytical characterization facilitates further study and potential use of these states in quantum protocols.

title: Correlation Functions For Quantum Dynamics Of Coupled Quasinormal Modes And Quantum Emitters Interacting Via Finite-delay Propagating Photons
authors: Robert Meiners Fuchs, Juanjuan Ren, Sebastian Franke, Stephen Hughes, And Marten Richter
abstract:
Author(s): Robert Meiners Fuchs, Juanjuan Ren, Sebastian Franke, Stephen Hughes, and Marten Richter

A time-dependent theory for the interactions between spatially separated lossy cavities in a homogeneous background medium using quantized quasinormal modes (QNMs) is presented. The cavities interact via a bath of traveling photons, described by nonbosonic operators that are orthogonal to the open-c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023725] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: Presents a time-dependent theory for interactions between lossy cavities and quantum emitters via propagating photons using quantized quasinormal modes.
motivation: To describe the quantum dynamics of spatially separated lossy cavities coupled through a photonic bath, which is relevant for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses quantized quasinormal modes and nonbosonic operators to model the interaction with traveling photons, deriving correlation functions.
result: Provides a time-dependent theory enabling the calculation of correlation functions for such coupled cavity-emitter systems.
conclusion: The theory can be used to study quantum dynamics of coupled cavity-emitter systems with finite-delay propagating photons.

title: Robust Universal Photon Blockade In A Bimodal Jaynes-Cummings Model Via Kerr Nonlinearity
authors: Guohao Chang, Hunduz Halemjan, Shangyun Liu, Raziya Anwar, And Ahmad Abliz
abstract:
Author(s): Guohao Chang, Hunduz Halemjan, Shangyun Liu, Raziya Anwar, and Ahmad Abliz

Universal photon blockade, which enables strong antibunching across a broad nonlinear parameter range, is demonstrated in a two-mode Jaynes-Cummings model incorporating third-order Kerr nonlinearity. Realization of this universal photon blockade is attributed to the cooperative effects of field-atom…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023727] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates universal photon blockade in a bimodal Jaynes-Cummings model with Kerr nonlinearity, achieving robust antibunching across a broad nonlinear parameter range.
motivation: Photon blockade is crucial for generating single photons, but typical implementations are sensitive to parameter variations. The authors aim to realize a robust universal photon blockade that works over a wide range of nonlinear parameters.
method: The authors analyze a two-mode Jaynes-Cummings model with third-order Kerr nonlinearity. They use a quantum master equation approach and derive analytical conditions for strong antibunching. Through numerical simulations, they show that both modes can exhibit photon blockade simultaneously, with robustness to detunings and nonlinear strengths, leading to a universal blockade condition.

title: Krylov Complexity And Fidelity Susceptibility In Two-band Hamiltonians
authors: Rishav Chaudhuri, Ayush Raj, Soham Ray, And Sai Satyam Samal
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Chaudhuri, Ayush Raj, Soham Ray, and Sai Satyam Samal

We investigate Krylov spread complexity for the ground state of two-band Hamiltonians, where the reference state is a generic state on the Bloch sphere. The spread complexity is obtained by using a purely geometric formulation in terms of Bloch sphere data without constructing the circuit Hamiltonia…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125134] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Krylov spread complexity for ground states of two-band Hamiltonians using a geometric formulation on the Bloch sphere, providing insights into complexity growth without explicit circuit construction.
motivation: The study aims to understand how Krylov complexity, a quantum chaos indicator, is determined by simple geometric features of two-band systems, which are fundamental models in condensed matter.
method: The authors use a purely geometric formulation of Krylov complexity based on Bloch sphere data, avoiding explicit circuit Hamiltonian construction, and apply it to generic reference states.
result: They derive relationships between spread complexity and Bloch sphere geometry, suggesting that complexity is constrained by the curvature and topology of the underlying state space.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that Krylov complexity in two-band Hamiltonians can be understood through simple geometric principles, offering a new perspective on complexity in quantum systems.

title: Multilevel Spectral Navigation With Geometric Diabatic-adiabatic Control
authors: Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, And Maximilian Rimbach-Russ
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, and Maximilian Rimbach-Russ

A geometric control framework is presented that leverages a parameterized metric space to smoothly interpolate between diabatic and adiabatic quantum dynamics for state transfer in multilevel systems. By mapping single-parameter pulse shaping to routing along geometric trajectories, the method enables high-fidelity quantum information processing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032034] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a geometric control framework for high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems by smoothly interpolating between diabatic and adiabatic dynamics.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity quantum information processing, especially for multilevel systems where simple pulses often fail.
method: Uses a parameterized metric space to map pulse shaping to geometric trajectories, enabling continuous interpolation between diabatic and adiabatic control regimes.
result: Demonstrates that this geometric control approach yields high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel systems.
conclusion: Provides a versatile and robust control framework applicable to various quantum platforms, potentially improving gate fidelity and coherence in multilevel qubit systems.

title: Sources Of Nonlinearity Of A Driven Carbon Nanotube Electromechanical Resonator
authors: Sofia Sevitz, Kushagra Aggarwal, Jorge Tabanera-Bravo, Juliette Monsel, Florian Vigneau, Federico Fedele, Joe Dunlop, Juan M. R. Parrondo, Gerard J. Milburn, Janet Anders, Natalia Ares, And Federico Cerisola
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Sevitz, Kushagra Aggarwal, Jorge Tabanera-Bravo, Juliette Monsel, Florian Vigneau, Federico Fedele, Joe Dunlop, Juan M. R. Parrondo, Gerard J. Milburn, Janet Anders, Natalia Ares, and Federico Cerisola

Nanoelectromechanical resonators provide an ideal platform for investigating the interplay between electron transport and nonlinear mechanical motion. Externally driven suspended carbon nanotubes, containing an electrostatically defined quantum dot, are especially promising. These devices possess tw…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033237] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the sources of nonlinearity in a driven carbon nanotube electromechanical resonator with a quantum dot, providing insights into the interplay between electron transport and mechanical motion.
motivation: Understanding nonlinearities in nanoelectromechanical resonators is crucial for their use in quantum thermodynamics and sensing applications.
method: The authors analyze a model of a carbon nanotube resonator coupled to a quantum dot, deriving the equations of motion including nonlinear terms arising from the electromechanical coupling and electron transport.

title: Negative Hybridization: A Potential Cure For Braiding With Imperfect Majorana Modes
authors: Cole Peeters, Themba Hodge, And Stephan Rachel
abstract:
Author(s): Cole Peeters, Themba Hodge, and Stephan Rachel

The degeneracy breaking hybridization between Majorana zero modes leads to unwanted dynamic phase accumulation and thus introduces error to topological quantum gates. In certain regimes, the effects of hybridization can be cancelled by the inclusion of an equal amount of “negative hybridization” that has been demonstrated via simulation to drastically reduce dynamic errors in
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032032] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to cancel hybridization errors in Majorana braiding by introducing 'negative hybridization', which improves gate fidelity in topological quantum computation.
motivation: Hybridization between Majorana zero modes causes dynamic phase errors in topological quantum gates, and existing approaches do not fully mitigate this issue.
method: The authors propose adding an equal amount of 'negative hybridization' to cancel the effects of degeneracy breaking, and demonstrate its effectiveness via simulation.
result: Simulations show that this method drastically reduces dynamic errors in CNOT and other gates, improving gate performance.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical cure for braiding errors due to imperfect Majorana modes, potentially advancing fault-tolerant topological quantum computing.

title: Forecasting Quantum Observables: A Compressed Sensing Approach With Performance Guarantees
authors: Víctor Valls, Albert Akhriev, Olatz Sanz Larrarte, Javier Oliva Del Moral, Štěpán Šmíd, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Sergiy Zhuk, And Dmytro Mishagli
abstract:
Author(s): Víctor Valls, Albert Akhriev, Olatz Sanz Larrarte, Javier Oliva del Moral, Štěpán Šmíd, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Sergiy Zhuk, and Dmytro Mishagli

Quantum experiments end where noise takes over—but the dynamics don’t. A compressed sensing framework is presented for certifying the reliability of quantum observable forecasts.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032030] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A compressed sensing framework is introduced to certify the reliability of forecasting quantum observables under noise, with performance guarantees.
motivation: Quantum experiments are limited by noise, but the underlying dynamics continue; reliable prediction of quantum observables beyond noisy regimes is needed.
method: The authors develop a compressed sensing approach that reconstructs or predicts quantum observables from limited measurements, providing certified performance bounds.
result: The framework offers performance guarantees for forecasting quantum observables, enabling robust predictions even when experiments are affected by noise.
conclusion: This work advances quantum state estimation and observable prediction, contributing to quantum information processing under realistic noise conditions.

title: Realization Of Trapped Ion Dynamics In The Strong-field Regime And non-Markovianity
authors: Kamran Rehan, Hengchao Tu, Tadeu Tassis, Menglin Zou, Zihan Yin, Jing-Ning Zhang, Fernando L. Semião, And Kihwan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Kamran Rehan, Hengchao Tu, Tadeu Tassis, Menglin Zou, Zihan Yin, Jing-Ning Zhang, Fernando L. Semião, and Kihwan Kim

We experimentally investigate trapped ion dynamics in the strong-driving regime, where the Rabi frequency [MATH] is comparable to the vibrational mode frequency [MATH]. In the conventional weak-driving regime ([MATH]), the dynamics is well described by effective Hamiltonians for the carri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033214] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of trapped ion dynamics in the strong-driving regime, revealing non-Markovian behavior beyond the weak-driving effective Hamiltonian approximation.
motivation: To explore trapped ion dynamics when the Rabi frequency is comparable to the vibrational frequency, where standard weak-driving approximations break down, and to observe non-Markovian effects.
method: Uses a trapped ion system under strong driving fields and measures the resulting dynamics, comparing to theoretical models.
result: Observes non-Markovian dynamics and deviations from Markovian behavior in the strong-driving regime.
conclusion: Provides experimental insights into strong-field ion dynamics and non-Markovian quantum processes, relevant for quantum control and open quantum systems.

title: Collective Early-time Spontaneous Decay Of A Cold Atomic Ensemble From The Single To Multiple Excitation Regime
authors: Daniel Benedicto Orenes, Naudson Lucas Lopes Matias, Apoorva Apoorva, Antoine Glicenstein, Raphaël Saint-Jalm, And Robin Kaiser
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Benedicto Orenes, Naudson Lucas Lopes Matias, Apoorva Apoorva, Antoine Glicenstein, Raphaël Saint-Jalm, and Robin Kaiser

In this work, we present a numerical and experimental investigation of the collective early-time decay rates of an optically dense cold atomic cloud supporting a large number of excitations. We prepare the atomic ensemble by driving the system to its steady state with varying Rabi frequencies $\math…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033199] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: An experimental and numerical study of collective early-time decay in cold atomic ensembles with multiple excitations, revealing deviations from single-excitation superradiance.
motivation: Understanding collective decay is crucial for atomic-ensemble-based quantum memories, where multi-excitation effects impact storage and retrieval efficiencies.
method: The authors prepared an optically dense cold atomic cloud in steady state with varying Rabi frequencies, measured early-time decay rates, and compared them with numerical simulations.
result: They observed that for large excitation numbers, the collective decay rate scales differently and exhibits deviations from the single-excitation behavior, characterized over a range of parameters.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into multi-excitation superradiance, offering practical guidance for designing efficient quantum memories based on atomic ensembles.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Presents a model-free method to measure irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings, providing an accessible tool for characterizing nonequilibrium behavior.
motivation: There is a need for versatile and accessible experimental methods to quantify irreversibility in small, stochastic, time-dependent systems.
method: The method categorizes single-molecule displacements to infer irreversibility without relying on specific models, using position recordings as input.
result: The approach offers a practical way to measure irreversibility in continuous systems, validated experimentally.
conclusion: This model-free technique extends the ability to probe nonequilibrium thermodynamics in small systems, useful for a wide range of experimental settings.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses microwave spectroscopy via circuit QED to characterize few-carrier states and spin/valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, advancing qubit readout control.
motivation: Understanding spin and valley blockade in graphene quantum dots is essential for developing spin/valley qubits, but high-resolution spectroscopy was lacking.
method: The authors employ circuit quantum electrodynamics to perform microwave spectroscopy of few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots, detecting spin and valley blockade.
result: They achieve high-resolution spectroscopy and identify signatures of Pauli spin and valley blockade, demonstrating the potential for qubit control and readout.
conclusion: The results establish microwave spectroscopy as a powerful tool for characterizing graphene quantum dots and pave the way for advanced qubit control in this platform.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in distributed quantum sensing networks, presenting both achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: In multi-node quantum sensing networks, protecting the privacy of the estimated parameters is crucial, yet the fundamental limits of such private estimation are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the problem through constructive protocols that enable private estimation and derive no-go theorems that establish limitations, providing a comprehensive characterization.
result: They demonstrate that private estimation is achievable under certain conditions, while also revealing fundamental restrictions that cannot be overcome.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational framework for privacy in continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing, guiding future protocol design and practical implementations.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy detects charging energies in quantum dots by exploiting nuclear spin response, relevant for spin qubit characterization.
motivation: Characterizing charging energies in quantum dots is essential for optimizing spin qubit devices, but existing methods may have limitations. Nuclear spin magnetism offers a novel probe to address this.
method: The paper employs nuclear spin magnetism, likely through nuclear magnetic resonance or related techniques, to measure the response of nuclear spins to charging events in quantum dots, enabling the detection of charging energies.
result: The proposed strategy successfully detects charging energies, potentially providing improved sensitivity or accuracy compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This method offers a valuable new tool for investigating quantum dot spin qubits, contributing to better understanding and optimization of such qubit platforms.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to significantly improve the accuracy of Hamiltonian simulation by injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, enabling lower circuit depth for a given target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is crucial for quantum computing, and product formulas are a common approach, but their accuracy is often limited, requiring deep circuits. The authors aim to improve the efficiency of such simulations.
method: They propose to add auxiliary terms to standard product formulas, which correct errors without significant overhead, thus enhancing the accuracy of the simulation.
result: The improved product formulas achieve substantially lower circuit depth for a given accuracy compared to standard formulas, as demonstrated both theoretically and numerically.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and efficient way to improve Hamiltonian simulation, which is beneficial for quantum algorithms and classical simulations of quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols using long-lived nuclear memories in defect centers.
method: Uses repeated entanglement transfer between qubits and qudits within defect centers.
result: A universal scheme that accumulates entanglement between nuclear memory qudits.
conclusion: Paves the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication.

title: Absence Of Quasi-Majorana False Positives In Full-Shell Hybrid Nanowires
authors: Carlos Payá, César Robles, Pablo San-Jose, And Elsa Prada
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Payá, César Robles, Pablo San-Jose, and Elsa Prada

Tunneling spectroscopy cannot be used as an unambiguous detection tool for Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in conventional partial-shell nanowires. The presence of smooth confinement at the end of the hybrid wire (among other sources of disorder) can create exponentially pinned zero-energy states, called…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 096606] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that full-shell hybrid nanowires do not exhibit quasi-Majorana false positives, providing a more reliable platform for detecting Majorana zero modes.
motivation: Tunneling spectroscopy in partial-shell nanowires can be ambiguous due to quasi-Majorana states. Full-shell nanowires are proposed as an alternative; this paper tests their reliability.
method: The authors theoretically analyze full-shell hybrid nanowires, modeling the confinement and disorder to check for spurious zero-energy states.
result: They find that smooth confinement in full-shell nanowires does not generate exponentially pinned zero-energy states, thus eliminating quasi-Majorana false positives.
conclusion: Full-shell nanowires are a promising platform for unambiguous Majorana detection, which is crucial for topological quantum computing.

title: Propagation Of Two-photon Zernike States In Atmospheric Turbulence
authors: Hakob Avetisyan And Vahagn Abgaryan
abstract:
Author(s): Hakob Avetisyan and Vahagn Abgaryan

We analyze propagation and detection of two-photon states expanded in Zernike modes through atmospheric turbulence using the extended Huygens-Fresnel formalism. For spontaneous parametric down-conversion states prepared with a single Zernike pump mode, we analytically reduce the eight-dimensional co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023730] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: 分析双光子Zernike态在大气湍流中的传播与检测，使用扩展Huygens-Fresnel形式推导解析结果。
motivation: 理解大气湍流对量子通信的影响，以优化自由空间量子信道。
method: 利用扩展Huygens-Fresnel形式，对八维关联函数进行解析简化，计算传播后的两光子态。
result: 给出了Zernike模式在湍流中传播后的量子态表达式，并分析了检测保真度。
conclusion: Zernike态在湍流中的传播特性表明其可用于自由空间量子通信，但需考虑湍流退化效应。

title: Dynamical Imaginarity Measures Induced By Channel Divergences
authors: Peihua Tian And Yuan Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Peihua Tian and Yuan Sun

Based on two types of channel divergences, we introduce four kinds of dynamical imaginarity measures, defined respectively by the deviation of a quantum channel from the set of real channels and from its conjugate channel. We show that they satisfy the desirable properties for a valid dynamical imag…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022462] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces four dynamical imaginarity measures based on channel divergences and verifies their validity.
motivation: Imaginarity is a quantum resource, but existing measures are mostly static; this work aims to provide measures for dynamical processes.
method: It defines measures by deviations of a quantum channel from the set of real channels and its conjugate channel, and checks their mathematical properties.
result: The proposed measures satisfy desirable properties for valid dynamical imaginarity measures.
conclusion: This provides new tools for studying imaginarity in quantum channels and may advance quantum resource theory.

title: Nonreciprocity In Three Optical Modes With non-Markovian Effects
authors: H. Yi, T. Z. Luan, W. Y. Hu, Zhi-Cheng Shi, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): H. Yi, T. Z. Luan, W. Y. Hu, Zhi-Cheng Shi, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

In this work, we construct a coupled cavity system consisting of three optical modes to obtain an effective Hamiltonian mediated by coherent and dissipative couplings via adiabatic elimination of a large dissipation mode. We investigate the interference of coherent and dissipative photon-photon coup…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023726] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal photon transport in a three-mode coupled cavity system driven by coherent and dissipative couplings, incorporating non-Markovian effects.
motivation: Achieving nonreciprocity is essential for routing and isolation in quantum networks; the interplay of coherent and dissipative couplings offers a potential mechanism without magnetic fields.
method: The authors construct an effective Hamiltonian for three optical modes by adiabatically eliminating a large dissipation mode, then analyze the interference between coherent and dissipative photon-photon couplings under non-Markovian conditions.
result: The system exhibits nonreciprocal behavior arising from the interference of coherent and dissipative pathways, with non-Markovian effects modifying the dynamics and potentially enhancing nonreciprocity.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable approach to nonreciprocal devices for quantum networks, with tunable behavior via non-Markovian parameters.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for connecting statistical mechanics with quantum dynamics, and the spectral form factor is a key diagnostic.
method: The authors employ analytical techniques to derive the spectral form factor, considering contributions at leading and next-to-leading order in time for all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal features and symmetry-class dependencies.
conclusion: The work advances theoretical understanding of quantum chaos and may inform studies of thermalization and information scrambling in many-body systems.

title: Qudit Gate Decomposition For Lattice Gauge Theories On Superconducting Radio-frequency Cavities
authors: Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu , Henry Lamm, And Andrea Maestri
abstract:
Author(s): Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu , Henry Lamm, and Andrea Maestri

In this work we investigate the effect of decomposition basis on primitive qudit gates on superconducting radio-frequency cavity-based quantum computers with applications to lattice gauge theory. Three approaches are tested: snap and displacement gates, ecd and single-qubit rotations [MATH], and o…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022460] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper evaluates different decomposition bases for primitive qudit gates on superconducting RF cavities, with a focus on optimizing lattice gauge theory simulations.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of qudit gate operations on superconducting radio-frequency cavity-based quantum computers, particularly for applications in lattice gauge theory.
method: Three decomposition approaches are tested: snap and displacement gates, ECD (echoed conditional displacement) with single-qubit rotations, and another method (likely a truncated basis).
result: The study reveals how the choice of decomposition basis affects the performance of primitive qudit gates, potentially identifying the most suitable approach for lattice gauge theory tasks.
conclusion: Selecting an appropriate decomposition basis is crucial for effective qudit gate implementation, thereby enhancing the viability of superconducting RF cavities for quantum simulation of gauge theories.

title: Fractional Power-law Decay In The Spontaneous Emission Of A Two-level System
authors: Hiroki Nakabayashi, Hayato Kinkawa, Takano Taira, And Naomichi Hatano
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Nakabayashi, Hayato Kinkawa, Takano Taira, and Naomichi Hatano

The authors reveal a fractional power-law decay in the spontaneous emission of a two-level system in the short- and long-time regimes. The fractional exponent is determined by the dispersion relation and spatial dimension of the environment.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020202] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reveals a fractional power-law decay in the spontaneous emission of a two-level system, with the exponent determined by the environment's dispersion relation and spatial dimension.
motivation: Understanding the decay dynamics of quantum systems coupled to structured environments is important for quantum optics and quantum information.
method: The authors analyze the spontaneous emission process analytically, deriving the decay law and identifying the fractional power-law behavior in short and long time regimes.
result: They find that the spontaneous emission decay follows a fractional power law whose exponent is governed by the dispersion relation and spatial dimension of the environment.
conclusion: This work provides insights into non-exponential decay behaviors and how environment structure influences quantum dynamics, relevant for open quantum systems and decoherence.

title: Polaritonic Machine Learning For Graph-based Data Analysis
authors: Yuan Wang, Stefano Scali, And Oleksandr Kyriienko

Photonic and polaritonic systems offer a fast and efficient platform for accelerating machine learning (ML) through physics-based computing. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 025305] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A study on using polaritonic systems for accelerating machine learning on graph data, focusing on necessary conditions for computational advantage.
motivation: Polaritonic systems offer fast and efficient physics-based computing for ML; need to identify features that provide computational advantage.
method: Likely theoretical analysis of polaritonic systems' nonlinear optical processes for ML tasks on graph data.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, covering theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, and Pauli propagation offers a systematic method to do so using Pauli operator dynamics.
method: The paper develops the Pauli propagation framework, including its theoretical foundations, software implementation, and application to various quantum simulation tasks.
result: It presents a complete account that enables practical simulation of quantum circuits, potentially useful for error correction, state characterization, and algorithm validation.
conclusion: The framework is a versatile tool for quantum simulation, aiding in the development and analysis of quantum algorithms and devices.

title: Nonreciprocal Landau-Zener Tunneling With Heat-bath Colored Noise
authors: Yi Cao And Jie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Cao and Jie Liu

In this work we investigate the effects of heat-bath-induced colored noise on nonreciprocal Landau-Zener tunneling. We perform numerical calculations of the instantaneous energy levels and find that noise induces stochastic fluctuations in these levels. Beyond such fluctuations, sufficiently large n…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022217] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically investigates how heat-bath-induced colored noise affects nonreciprocal Landau-Zener tunneling, finding that noise causes stochastic fluctuations in instantaneous energy levels and can significantly alter tunneling behavior.
motivation: Understanding the impact of realistic environmental noise on Landau-Zener tunneling is important for quantum control and computation, where colored noise is often present but not fully explored.
method: The authors perform numerical calculations of instantaneous energy levels for a system undergoing Landau-Zener tunneling under colored noise, presumably using master equations or stochastic Schrödinger equations.
result: Sufficiently large colored noise induces stochastic fluctuations in the energy levels and modifies the tunneling probability, potentially suppressing or enhancing nonreciprocal effects depending on noise parameters.
conclusion: Colored noise can substantially influence Landau-Zener tunneling, suggesting that realistic noise models must be considered in quantum device operation and thermal-noise-assisted control.

title: Entanglement In Elastic Electron Scattering: Perturbation Theory Misses Fundamental Aspects Of Bragg Scattering
authors: Stefan Löffler And Peter Schattschneider
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Löffler and Peter Schattschneider

Elastic electron scattering is one of the primary means of investigating materials on the atomic scale. It is usually described in a one-particle approach (the probe electron's evolution in a perturbative static potential), whereas we are dealing here with a two-body interaction between the probe an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033217] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates entanglement in elastic electron scattering, arguing that perturbative treatments miss fundamental aspects of Bragg scattering.
motivation: Elastic electron scattering is typically described via a single-particle perturbative potential, but the two-body interaction between probe and target may generate entanglement that is overlooked.
method: The authors analyze the scattering process likely using quantum mechanical formalisms that incorporate the two-body interaction and entanglement effects.
result: They demonstrate that perturbation theory fails to capture essential features of entanglement in the scattering, particularly in Bragg scattering.
conclusion: A more complete treatment beyond perturbation theory is required to properly describe elastic electron scattering.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
