tldr: Precision spectroscopy of ytterbium Rydberg molecules reveals electron-ion interactions, laying groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.
motivation: Understanding electron-ion interactions in Rydberg molecules is fundamental for atomic physics and may enable future quantum technologies.
method: The study employs high-precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules to measure and analyze energy level shifts and interactions.
result: The experiments provide detailed insights into electron-ytterbium interactions and molecular structure.
conclusion: The findings establish essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms, potentially relevant to quantum simulation and sensing platforms.

title: Path-Dependency And Emergent Computing Under Vectorial Driving
authors: C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, And M. van Hecke
abstract:
Author(s): C. M. Meulblok, A. Singh, M. Labousse, and M. van Hecke

A general framework unravels path dependencies across a wide range of driven complex materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031023] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general framework for understanding path dependencies in driven complex materials, enabling emergent computing behaviors.
motivation: Driven complex materials often display memory and path-dependent responses, but a unified understanding is lacking. The authors aim to provide a general framework to capture these phenomena and explore their computational potential.
method: The authors introduce a general framework that describes path dependencies under vectorial driving protocols, likely by mapping the response space and characterizing the accessible states.
result: The framework successfully unravels path dependencies across a wide range of driven materials, revealing common principles and enabling emergent computation.
conclusion: This work establishes a unified perspective on memory and computing in complex materials, which could have implications for information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Nonequilibrium Phases And Quantum Correlations In Synthetic Transport Models
authors: Uddhav Sen, Federico Carollo, And Sascha Wald
abstract:
Author(s): Uddhav Sen, Federico Carollo, and Sascha Wald

Quantum devices featuring midcircuit measurement and reset capabilities, such as quantum computers and dual-species Rydberg quantum simulators, enable the realization of quantum cellular automata. These systems evolve in discrete time following local updates implemented by unitary gates and allow fo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090402] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phases and quantum correlations in synthetic transport models realized by quantum cellular automata, which are enabled by midcircuit measurement and reset in quantum devices.
motivation: The work is motivated by the possibility of implementing quantum cellular automata in modern quantum devices, and understanding their nonequilibrium behavior and quantum correlations.
method: The authors analyze discrete-time evolution under local unitary gates of quantum cellular automata, focusing on transport models and their phase structure.
result: They identify nonequilibrium phases and characterize quantum correlations in these systems, providing insights into their dynamics.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the theory of quantum cellular automata but is not directly aligned with the core research interests, as such topics are explicitly listed as non-priority.

title: Interaction-driven Floquet Superfluidity In A Two-component Fermi Gas
authors: Ming-Yue Yang, Lin Wen, An-Chun Ji, And Qing Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Yue Yang, Lin Wen, An-Chun Ji, and Qing Sun

We investigate the pairing problem in a two-component Fermi gas subject to periodically modulated attractive interactions. For the two-body case, we construct the Floquet bound state and find that its quasienergy decreases with the (dimensionless) driving strength, a manifestation of the renormalize…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023325] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Floquet superfluidity in a two-component Fermi gas with periodically modulated attractive interactions, showing that driving can renormalize interactions and lead to many-body pairing.
motivation: To explore how periodic modulation of interactions can be used to engineer superfluidity in ultracold fermionic systems, potentially offering new ways to control quantum phases.
method: The authors analyze both two-body and many-body pairing by constructing Floquet bound states and examining the quasienergy spectrum, deriving effective interaction strengths and showing the emergence of superfluidity.

title: Phase-dependent Optical Response And Quantum Sensing Of A V-type Quantum Emitter Near A Graphene Monolayer
authors: Sofia Evangelou
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Evangelou

We investigate the phase-dependent optical response and sensing capabilities of a V-type quantum emitter positioned near a graphene monolayer. The graphene sheet creates an anisotropic electromagnetic environment that modifies the spontaneous emission rates and induces correlated decay between the t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023729] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a V-type quantum emitter near a graphene monolayer, showing phase-dependent optical response and quantum sensing capabilities.
motivation: To understand how a graphene monolayer affects the emission properties of a quantum emitter and to exploit this for quantum sensing.
method: The authors theoretically model the emitter's dynamics in the anisotropic electromagnetic environment induced by graphene, considering modified spontaneous emission and correlated decay.
result: They find that the optical response is phase-dependent and can be used for sensing applications.
conclusion: The graphene-emitter system offers a platform for quantum sensing with controllable optical response.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper integrates molecular spins with mechanical readout to achieve sensitive quantum sensing, detecting nanotesla magnetic fields and resolving local nuclear spectra.
motivation: To enable high-sensitivity magnetic field detection and local nuclear spectroscopy using molecular spin systems with mechanical detection.
method: The authors employ a mechanical readout approach, likely magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM), to detect the magnetic signals from molecular spins.
result: They successfully detected nanotesla-scale magnetic fields and resolved local nuclear spectra, demonstrating the effectiveness of the mechanical detection scheme.
conclusion: The work showcases the potential of combining molecular spins with mechanical readout for advanced quantum sensing applications.

title: Universality Classes Split By Strong And Weak Symmetries
authors: Jongjun M. Lee, Myung-Joong Hwang, And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Jongjun M. Lee, Myung-Joong Hwang, and Igor Boettcher

Dissipative phase transitions are strongly shaped by the symmetries of the Liouvillian, yet a clear understanding of the quantitative impact of weak and strong symmetries on critical behavior is presently lacking. We study a squeezed-photon model with single- and two-photon losses, realizing weak an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022469] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how weak and strong symmetries in dissipative phase transitions lead to distinct universality classes, using a squeezed-photon model with losses.
motivation: The impact of weak and strong symmetries on critical behavior in dissipative systems is not well understood, and this work aims to clarify their quantitative effects.
method: The authors study a squeezed-photon model with single- and two-photon losses, analyzing the Liouvillian's symmetries and critical behavior, likely through analytical and numerical techniques.
result: The study reveals that weak and strong symmetries yield different universality classes, indicating that symmetry type crucially determines critical exponents in dissipative phase transitions.
conclusion: Understanding the role of symmetry in dissipative critical phenomena is essential for classifying emergent behavior in open quantum systems, though the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamic applications.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: 定量评估了打破椭圆曲线加密货币所需的量子计算资源，并强调了向抗量子密码迁移的紧迫性。
motivation: 社区低估了量子计算机对加密货币的威胁，需要精确的资源估计来指导安全决策。
method: 基于Shor算法和量子纠错分析，估算破解椭圆曲线密码所需的物理资源（如逻辑量子比特数、时间等），并比较了不同后量子密码方案。
result: 发现实现攻击的量子计算机规模比预期更小、更近，对现有加密货币构成实际威胁。
conclusion: 加密货币必须及时迁移到抗量子密码算法，以防范未来量子攻击。

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.

motivation: 研究多模量子相变，特别是开放系统中的耗散相变行为，以理解量子多体系统的非平衡稳态。

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions in various parameter regimes, highlighting where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of matrix functions is essential for identifying problems where quantum computers could outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems across different parameter regimes, likely using quantum complexity theory frameworks and reductions.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity, offering insights into potential quantum advantage for specific matrix function problems.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the broader understanding of quantum computational complexity and indicate promising directions for quantum algorithmic development.

title: General Thermodynamic Approach For Diffusion On A Lattice
authors: M. A. Di Muro And M. Hoyuelos
abstract:
Author(s): M. A. Di Muro and M. Hoyuelos

This work presents a general thermodynamic approach to describe particle diffusion on a lattice, a model used to study transport processes in solids and on surfaces. By treating each lattice site as an open thermodynamic system, the effects of microscopic particle interactions are represented throug…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024152] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general thermodynamic framework for particle diffusion on a lattice by treating each site as an open system.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamic basis for diffusion models, connecting microscopic interactions to macroscopic transport behavior.

title: Eightfold Classification Of Superconducting Orders
authors: Alexander V. Balatsky And Saikat Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander V. Balatsky and Saikat Banerjee

Superconductivity begins when electrons bind into pairs. Because electrons are fermions, exchanging the two partners in a pair must flip the sign of its wavefunction — and that minus sign can be paid for in four different currencies: the pair’s spin, its spatial shape, its orbital character, and, less obviously, the relative time between the two electrons. Sharing one minus sign among four ± choices leaves exactly eight allowed kinds of Cooper pair. Balatsky and Banerjee show here that this eightfold rule is one face of a larger structure. A pair also has a center of mass — a place and a moment — and a superconductor can order in those as well. Taking internal shape (ρ), internal timing (τ), spatial modulation (R), and temporal modulation (T) as four independent axes builds the Berezinskii–Abrahams hypercube: a sixteen-corner map of superconducting order. BCS sits at the origin; each single axis recovers a familiar family —
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074511] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a hypercube classification of superconducting orders based on four binary axes: internal shape, internal timing, spatial modulation, and temporal modulation, yielding sixteen possible ordered states.
motivation: To provide a unified classification framework for superconducting orders, including exotic states like odd-frequency pairing and pair-density waves, and to identify unexplored hybrid states.
method: The authors define four independent binary degrees of freedom for Cooper pairs (internal shape, internal timing, spatial modulation, temporal modulation) and construct a hypercube where each corner represents a distinct superconducting order.
result: The framework reproduces known families (BCS, odd-frequency, FFLO, PDW) as single-axis excitations and reveals unexplored corners, including a fully hybridized state never visited.
conclusion: The hypercube serves as both a classification scheme and a search map for new superconducting phases, guiding future experimental and theoretical exploration.

We theoretically investigate the collisions between ultracold polar molecules in the presence of two lasers ensuring a Raman resonant transition on individual molecules to suppress photon scattering, taking the example of bosonic [MATH] molecules. By varying laser detuning…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033200] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates two-photon optical shielding to suppress inelastic collisions and photon scattering in ultracold polar molecules.
motivation: Ultracold polar molecules suffer from inelastic collisions and photon scattering that limit their lifetime; the authors aim to suppress these effects using two-photon Raman transitions.
method: They model collisions in the presence of two lasers that induce Raman resonance on individual molecules and analyze the effect of laser detuning on collision dynamics.
result: The two-photon optical shielding can effectively reduce losses due to inelastic collisions and photon scattering, as demonstrated for bosonic molecules.
conclusion: The proposed two-photon shielding scheme offers a promising approach to stabilize ultracold molecular gases.

title: Phonon-Activated Collective Hopping In A Superionic Phase
authors: Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, And Olivier Delaire
abstract:
Author(s): Hung-Min Lin, Mayanak K. Gupta, Niuchang Ouyang, Tyler Wilson, Artem Pogodin, Md Towhidur Rahman, Alexandra Zevalkink, J. Ross Stewart, Fanni Juranyi, Tao Hong, Yan Wu, Songxue Chi, Douglas L. Abernathy, and Olivier Delaire

Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improves the microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031046] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Observations of collective hopping in superionic agryodites improve microscopic understanding of transport in these materials.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanisms of ionic transport in superionic conductors, which are important for energy applications.
method: The study likely uses neutron scattering and/or other experimental techniques to probe phonon-activated collective hopping dynamics.
result: The paper reports direct observations of collective hopping behavior in superionic agryodite phases.
conclusion: The findings provide a better microscopic picture of superionic transport, which may inform the design of improved ionic conductors.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the robustness of real-space topology in moiré systems, establishing a band index and mapping wave functions onto a fictitious magnetic field derived from electronic textures.
motivation: To understand the topological properties of nonidealized moiré systems, which are relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly connected to the user's research interests.
method: The authors perform a topological analysis of real-space electronic textures, defining a robust band index and constructing a fictitious magnetic field from the texture.
result: They establish that the band index is robust and show that wave functions can be mapped onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for characterizing topology in realistic moiré systems, but it does not align with the user's focus areas in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Standard Model Of Electromagnetism And Chirality In Crystals
authors: R. Winkler And U. Zülicke
abstract:
Author(s): R. Winkler and U. Zülicke

A comprehensive symmetry-based classification identifies 12 fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures across five polar and five chiral categories, providing a complete taxonomy to predict and engineer next-generation multifunctional materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031039] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a symmetry-based classification of 12 crystal structure types across polar and chiral categories, aiming to guide the design of multifunctional materials.
motivation: To understand and predict the electromagnetic properties of crystals based on their symmetry, particularly focusing on chirality and polarity.
method: A comprehensive symmetry-based classification was performed, identifying distinct categories of crystal structures.
result: Twelve fundamentally distinct types of crystal structures were identified, spanning five polar and five chiral categories.
conclusion: The classification provides a complete taxonomy to predict and engineer next-generation multifunctional materials.

title: Coulomb Screening Of Superconductivity In Magic-Angle Graphene
authors: Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe de Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, And Alexey I. Berdyugin
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe De Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, and Alexey I. Berdyugin

Metallic layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions and reveal that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than conventional atomic vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031040] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Metallic screening layers suppress Coulomb interactions in magic-angle graphene, showing that its superconductivity arises from electronic interactions rather than phonons.
motivation: To determine the pairing mechanism (electron-phonon vs. electron-electron) behind superconductivity in magic-angle graphene.
method: Place metallic layers near magic-angle graphene to screen Coulomb interactions and measure the effect on the superconducting transition.
result: Suppressing Coulomb interactions weakens superconductivity, indicating that electronic interactions are the driving force.
conclusion: Superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is driven by electronic interactions, not conventional phonon-mediated pairing.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a unified symmetry classification using spin space groups to predict a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase with continuous spin polarization variation.
motivation: To unify classification of magnetic orders via spin space groups and predict novel magnetic phases.
method: Employing spin space group symmetry classification to analyze magnetic structures and their electronic band properties.
result: Predicts a coplanar even-wave phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.
conclusion: The framework provides a new classification scheme and theoretical prediction for magnetic phases.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution In Mg-Ag-Sb For Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao
abstract:
Author(s): Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, and Jun Mao

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031035] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phase evolution in Mg-Ag-Sb thermoelectric material to enable thermally recoverable performance.
motivation: Thermal degradation limits thermoelectric device stability, so understanding phase changes could enable recovery.
method: Experimental and computational analysis of phase transitions and annealing effects.
result: Low-temperature annealing reverses thermal degradation in MgAgSb.
conclusion: Design principles for thermally recoverable thermoelectrics are proposed.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the strain-tunable anomalous Hall effect in hexagonal MnTe, an altermagnet, and demonstrates that uniaxial strain can isolate a single magnetic domain and modify the Berry curvature, leading to a sharp anomalous Hall effect and sign reversal.
motivation: To understand and control the anomalous Hall effect in altermagnets, which are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications.
method: The authors applied uniaxial strain to single crystals of hexagonal MnTe and measured the Hall effect as a function of strain and temperature, along with neutron scattering to characterize the magnetic structure.
result: Uniaxial strain was found to isolate a single magnetic domain, resulting in a sharp anomalous Hall effect. The sign of the anomalous Hall effect could be reversed by tuning the strain, which was attributed to modifications in the electronic Berry curvature.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that strain is an effective tool to control the magnetic domain structure and the anomalous Hall effect in altermagnets, which could be relevant for future spintronic devices.

title: Fast Algorithm For 2d Rigidity Percolation
authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Javerzat and Daniele Notarmuzi

An algorithm for simulating the rigidity percolation transition, based on novel theoretical results, overcomes previous size limitations and enables the highly precise characterization of its universality classes, shedding new light on rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031032] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: A fast algorithm based on novel theoretical results enables precise simulation and characterization of 2D rigidity percolation universality classes.
motivation: To overcome previous size limitations in simulating rigidity percolation and to accurately determine its universality classes, thereby illuminating rigidity transitions in amorphous systems.
method: The authors propose an algorithm grounded in novel theoretical insights that efficiently simulates the rigidity percolation transition in 2D.
result: The algorithm overcomes prior size constraints, enabling highly precise characterization of universality classes and providing new insights into rigidity percolation.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of rigidity percolation and offers a computational tool for studying amorphous materials.

title: Observation Of Correlated Plasmons In Low-Valence Nickelates
authors: Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, And M. P. M. Dean
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Shen, W. He, J. Sears, Xuefei Guo, Xiangpeng Luo, A. Roll, J. Li, J. Pelliciari, Xi He, I. Božovič, Junjie Zhang, J. F. Mitchell, V. Bisogni, M. Mitrano, S. Johnston, and M. P. M. Dean

Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering measurements reveal propagating plasmons in the low-valence nickelate Pr
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031031] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of correlated plasmons in low-valence nickelates via resonant inelastic x-ray scattering, revealing dynamics distinct from cuprates.
motivation: Understanding the electronic properties of nickelate superconductors and their relation to cuprates is important, and this study investigates collective excitations like plasmons.
method: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) was used to measure density-density correlations and observe propagating plasmons in Pr4Ni3O8.
result: Correlated plasmons with dynamics distinct from cuprates were found, providing insights into strong coupling effects in nickelates.
conclusion: The results highlight unique electronic behavior in nickelates and may inform models of unconventional superconductivity.

title: Mechanochemical Nano-Writing Of An Atomically Thin Metal
authors: Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, And Robert W. Carpick
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Zhang, Yanyu Jia, Atanu Samanta, Yutian Bao, Haosen Guan, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Guangming Cheng, Ting Liu, Cangyu Qu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nan Yao, Ashlie Martini, Leslie Schoop, Andrew M. Rappe, Sanfeng Wu, and Robert W. Carpick

A large stress generated by a small tip drives a reaction between two materials in an 2D encapsulated space to produce a new material with interesting electronic properties that can be written into patterns as small as 50 nm.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031029] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a mechanochemical nano-writing technique to create atomically thin metal patterns as small as 50 nm using a stress-driven reaction in a 2D encapsulated space.
motivation: To enable nanoscale fabrication of atomically thin materials with controlled electronic properties for potential device applications.
method: A sharp tip applies large mechanical stress to trigger a reaction between two materials confined in a 2D encapsulated space, producing a new atomically thin metal layer.
result: The technique successfully creates atomically thin metal patterns with feature sizes down to 50 nm, and the produced material exhibits interesting electronic properties.
conclusion: This mechanochemical approach offers a novel route for nano-lithography of 2D materials, but it is not directly aligned with the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Riemannian Geometric Classification And Emergent Phenomena Of Magnetic Textures
authors: Koki Shinada And Naoto Nagaosa
abstract:
Author(s): Koki Shinada and Naoto Nagaosa

A classification framework based on differential geometry introduces geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron equations of motion in complex magnetic textures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031026] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: A differential geometry framework classifies magnetic textures using new chiralities, revealing a quantum geometric effect that modifies electron motion.
motivation: To understand and classify complex magnetic textures beyond simple spin chirality, and to explore their quantum geometric consequences.
method: Introduces Riemannian geometric classification with geodesic and torsional scalar spin chiralities, and derives modified electron equations of motion.
result: New quantum geometric effects in electron dynamics are identified for complex magnetic textures.
conclusion: Provides a novel classification framework and deepens understanding of emergent phenomena in magnetic textures.

title: Predicting Liquid Properties And Behavior Via Droplet Pinch-off And Machine Learning
authors: Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, And José Rafael Castrejón-Pita
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtao Wang, Qiwei Chen, C. Ricardo Constante-Amores, Denise Gorse, Alfonso Arturo Castrejón-Pita, and José Rafael Castrejón-Pita

A powerful method allows hard to measure properties like viscosity and surface tension to be determined from a single, high-speed snapshot.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031021] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning on high-speed droplet pinch-off snapshots to predict liquid properties like viscosity and surface tension.
motivation: To provide a simple and fast method for measuring hard-to-measure liquid properties from a single image.
method: The authors train a machine learning model on high-speed images of droplet pinch-off to predict viscosity and surface tension.
result: The model successfully predicts liquid properties from a single snapshot.
conclusion: The approach offers a powerful and practical tool for fluid property measurement.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation For Open Systems: Emergence Of Exceptional Points In Excitonic Spectra From First Principles
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, And Gianluca Stefanucci
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, and Gianluca Stefanucci

Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031020] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems, predicting exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides due to engineered photonic environments.
motivation: To predict and control exceptional points in excitonic spectra for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.
method: The authors derive a non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter equation for open systems, incorporating coupling to photonic environments.
result: They find that exceptional points emerge in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides under engineered photonic environments.
conclusion: This provides a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Limits Of Inference In Complex Systems: When Stochastic Models Become Indistinguishable
authors: Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, And Sandro Azaele
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, and Sandro Azaele

A path-inference framework quantifies data resolution limits that render distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements that maximize information extraction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031015] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a path-inference framework to quantify data resolution limits that make distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable, and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements to maximize information extraction.
motivation: In complex systems, limited data resolution can obscure differences between stochastic models, making them empirically indistinguishable; the authors aim to quantify these limits.
method: They develop a path-inference framework that quantifies data resolution limits, likely using information-theoretic or likelihood-based measures.
result: They demonstrate that distinct stochastic models can become indistinguishable due to finite resolution and provide guidelines for experimental design to maximize information extraction.
conclusion: The framework reveals fundamental limits of inference in complex systems and informs experimental design.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper engineers special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules to suppress electromagnetic noise, enabling high-precision probes of physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: Precision measurements of beyond-standard-model phenomena, such as the electron electric dipole moment, are limited by electromagnetic noise, which reduces sensitivity.
method: The authors design special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules that cancel leading sources of electromagnetic noise while preserving sensitivity to new physics.
result: They demonstrate suppression of electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while maintaining high sensitivity to beyond-standard-model signals.
conclusion: This engineering approach enables more precise molecular measurements, advancing the search for new physics.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental evidence for a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 via pump-probe spectroscopy.
motivation: To identify and characterize fractional topological insulators, which are exotic quantum states of matter.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy on a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: Observation of an out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response, providing experimental signatures of a putative fractional topological insulator.
conclusion: The observed signatures suggest that twisted MoTe2 bilayers may host a fractional topological insulator phase.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical framework for quantum fields backreacting on classical space-time, bridging quantum mechanics and general relativity.
motivation: To reconcile quantum mechanics and Einstein's gravity by allowing space-time to remain classical while matter is quantum, and to test if space-time requires a quantum description.
method: The paper develops covariant path integrals to describe the interaction between quantum fields and classical space-time, including backreaction effects.
result: It provides a consistent mathematical framework that could yield testable predictions about the classicality of space-time.
conclusion: This framework offers a way to experimentally probe whether space and time are fundamentally classical or quantum.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: ARPES study of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not present at the Fermi level, suggesting it is not essential for superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure of nickelate superconductors and clarify the role of the out-of-plane nickel orbital in the superconducting mechanism.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on bilayer nickelate thin films with varying strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band moves with strain and doping but does not cross the Fermi level, indicating it is not directly involved in the superconducting state.
conclusion: The out-of-plane nickel orbital is not required for superconductivity, pointing to other electronic states as the key contributors.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A gradient-free quantum optimization approach using coherent time evolution, which outperforms gradient-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.
motivation: Gradient-based quantum optimization methods often suffer from barren plateaus and high query complexity, motivating a gradient-free alternative.
method: The paper introduces a gradient-free algorithm that uses coherent simulation of time evolution to explore the optimization landscape without computing gradients.
result: The method achieves lower query complexity and greater robustness to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent-based approaches.
conclusion: Gradient-free dynamical simulation is a promising technique for quantum optimization, offering practical advantages in certain settings.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a cluster-corrected belief propagation algorithm for tensor network contraction that provides polynomial-time complexity with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Exact tensor network contraction is computationally hard; approximate methods like belief propagation lack accuracy for networks with loops. The authors aim to develop a systematic, polynomial-time approximation with guaranteed error bounds.
method: The method augmentates standard belief propagation with cluster corrections, presumably by incorporating higher-order correlations via local clusters, and derives rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves exponential convergence with increasing cluster size while maintaining polynomial computational cost.
conclusion: This work offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach to tensor network contraction, potentially beneficial for quantum many-body simulations.

title: Correlated Insulator At The Surface Of The Polar Metal ${\mathrm{Ca}}_{3}{\text{Ru}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Daniel Halliday, Izidor Benedičič, Andela Zivanovic, Masahiro Naritsuka, Brendan Edwards, Tommaso Antonelli, Naoki Kikugawa, Dmitry A. Sokolov, Craig Polley, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Georg Held, Phil D. C. King, And Peter Wahl
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Halliday, Izidor Benedičič, Andela Zivanovic, Masahiro Naritsuka, Brendan Edwards, Tommaso Antonelli, Naoki Kikugawa, Dmitry A. Sokolov, Craig Polley, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Georg Held, Phil D. C. King, and Peter Wahl

We investigate the electronic structure at the surface of the correlated oxide [MATH], a low-symmetry ruthenate oxide which hosts an unconventional polar-metal phase. From a combination of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and scanning tunneling …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 096503] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a correlated insulating state at the surface of the polar metal Ca3Ru2O7, characterized by ARPES and STM.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and possible correlated phases at the surface of a low-symmetry ruthenate oxide hosting a polar metal phase.
method: The authors combined angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) to probe the surface electronic states.
result: The measurements reveal an insulating gap at the surface, indicating a correlated insulator state distinctly different from the metallic bulk.
conclusion: The surface of Ca3Ru2O7 exhibits a correlated insulating phase that is not present in the bulk, highlighting the importance of surface effects in correlated oxides.

title: Curvature-induced Bound States In Quantum Wires
authors: Tim Bergmann, Benjamin Schwager, And Jamal Berakdar
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Bergmann, Benjamin Schwager, and Jamal Berakdar

A classical particle under spatial constraints is strictly confined to live on a specific space manifold or path, but this assumption is incompatible with the zero-point fluctuations of a quantum particle. One way to treat quantum mechanics under constraints is the confinement potential approach (CP…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033228] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates bound states induced by curvature in quantum wires using a confinement potential approach.
motivation: To understand how geometric constraints affect quantum particle behavior, going beyond classical confinement assumptions.
method: The authors employ the confinement potential approach (CPA) to model quantum mechanics under spatial constraints.
result: They demonstrate that curvature gives rise to bound states in quantum wires, with properties dependent on the wire geometry.
conclusion: Curvature-induced bound states are a genuine quantum effect that must be considered in nanoscale wire systems.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to derive the generalization error of a deep neural network near the interpolation threshold.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the behavior of deep learning models in the overparameterized regime using tools from statistical physics.
method: They analyze a deep fully connected neural network via random matrix theory and statistical physics techniques, focusing on the interpolation point.
result: They uncover mechanisms governing feature learning propagation across layers and provide a theoretical characterization of the generalization error.
conclusion: The study offers insights into deep learning from a statistical physics perspective, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics of information processing, or any of the specified research directions.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian spectral topology using a cold Rydberg gas as a dissipative many-body platform.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in non-Hermitian systems, which are less understood than Hermitian counterparts, using a controllable many-body platform.
method: A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body system, and non-Hermitian spectral topology is mapped out by measuring winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
result: The experiment reveals interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological features.
conclusion: Cold Rydberg gases serve as a promising platform for studying non-Hermitian topological physics and related many-body dissipative dynamics.

title: Topological Defect Propagation To Classify Knitted Fabrics
authors: Daisuke S. Shimamoto, Keiko Shimamoto, Sonia Mahmoudi, And Samuel Poincloux
abstract:
Author(s): Daisuke S. Shimamoto, Keiko Shimamoto, Sonia Mahmoudi, and Samuel Poincloux

The ability of a fabric to be knitted into a textile can be determined on the basis of the topology of its pattern.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031006] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses topological defect propagation to classify the knitability of fabric patterns.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how the topology of a knitting pattern determines whether it can be successfully knitted into a textile.
method: They likely model knitted fabrics as topological structures and analyze the propagation of defects to determine knitability.
result: The paper provides a classification based on topological properties, linking pattern topology to fabric feasibility.
conclusion: Topological criteria can predict the ability to knit a given pattern, offering a new framework for textile design.

title: Strain-Tuned Nodal Superconductivity In The Charge-Ordered Kagome Metal ${\mathrm{CsV}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$
authors: Yusuke Takeuchi, Akito Kobayashi, Saki Uchida, Takumi Nagao, Seigo Ogawa, Rui Zhou, Shinji Kawasaki, Fei Song, Hao Ni, Yong Zhao, And Guo-Qing Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Takeuchi, Akito Kobayashi, Saki Uchida, Takumi Nagao, Seigo Ogawa, Rui Zhou, Shinji Kawasaki, Fei Song, Hao Ni, Yong Zhao, and Guo-qing Zheng

The ground state of CsV
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 096003] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Strain-tuned nodal superconductivity in the kagome metal CsV3Sb5 reveals two degenerate superconducting ground states.
motivation: To investigate the unconventional superconducting state in charge-ordered kagome metals and the effect of strain.
method: Experimental tuning of superconductivity via strain, likely through transport measurements.
result: The ground state consists of two degenerate superconducting states with nodal behavior.
conclusion: The work highlights the complex interplay between charge order, strain, and superconductivity in kagome systems.

title: Sign Problem Landscape Of Dimer, Loop, And Ground-State Sectors Of A U(1) Quantum Link Model
authors: Pallabi Dey, Debasish Banerjee, And Emilie Huffman
abstract:
Author(s): Pallabi Dey, Debasish Banerjee, and Emilie Huffman

The fermion sign problem poses a formidable challenge to the use of Monte Carlo methods for lattice gauge theories with dynamical fermionic matter fields. A meron-cluster algorithm recently formulated for gauge fields represented as spin-[MATH] quantum links coupled to a single flavor of staggered fe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 090404] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the sign problem in a U(1) quantum link model and demonstrates that a meron-cluster algorithm can overcome it in dimer, loop, and ground-state sectors.
motivation: The sign problem hinders Monte Carlo simulations of lattice gauge theories with dynamical fermions.
method: The authors apply a meron-cluster algorithm to a U(1) quantum link model with staggered fermions.
result: They analyze the sign problem in different sectors and find conditions under which it is absent.
conclusion: The work provides insights into sign-problem-free simulations of quantum link models.

title: Diagnostic Consistency Tests Of The Concordance Cosmology
authors: S. M. Koksbang And A. Heinesen
abstract:
Author(s): S. M. Koksbang and A. Heinesen

The [MATH] cold dark matter cosmological model faces increasingly significant and robust tensions among independent cosmological probes, prompting renewed scrutiny of its foundational assumptions. While general relativity and the nature of darkenergy are now routinely tested with cosmological …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 091001] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes diagnostic consistency tests for the concordance cosmology model to address tensions among cosmological probes.
motivation: To scrutinize foundational assumptions of the standard cosmological model in light of significant and robust tensions among independent probes.
method: Likely employs statistical consistency tests on cosmological datasets to evaluate the concordance model's assumptions.
result: Probably reveals inconsistencies or tensions that challenge the standard model's validity.
conclusion: Discusses implications for dark energy and general relativity, suggesting need for revised cosmological models.

title: Search For Gamma-Ray Spectral Lines From Dark Matter Annihilation With The H.e.s.s. Inner Galaxy Survey
authors: F. Aharonian et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): F. Aharonian et al. (H.E.S.S. Collaboration)

A 500-hour survey of the Galactic Center by the H.E.S.S. telescope array has set the most stringent limits to date on TeV dark matter line annihilation cross sections.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 091002] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the most stringent limits to date on TeV dark matter line annihilation cross sections using a 500-hour H.E.S.S. survey of the Galactic Center.
motivation: The search for gamma-ray spectral lines from dark matter annihilation is a key method for indirect dark matter detection, as such lines would provide a smoking-gun signal.
method: The H.E.S.S. telescope array observed the Galactic Center for 500 hours, and the data were analyzed to search for monoenergetic gamma-ray lines that would result from dark matter annihilation into two photons.
result: No significant gamma-ray line signal was found, and the resulting upper limits on the annihilation cross section are the most stringent obtained to date in the TeV mass range.
conclusion: The null result constrains dark matter models predicting line-like annihilation signatures, but does not rule out all dark matter candidates.

title: Evidence Of $ZZγ$ Production And Observation Of $4ℓγ$ In Proton-Proton Collisions At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: A. Hayrapetyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Hayrapetyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

Evidence of the production of two [MATH] bosons and a photon in proton-proton collisions is reported for the first time in CMS. The analysis uses data collected by the CMS experiment between 2016 and 2018 at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\te…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 091805] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports evidence for ZZγ production and observation of 4ℓγ in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, a measurement of a rare Standard Model process.
motivation: To study rare multi-boson production processes, which test the Standard Model and could reveal new physics.
method: Analysis of CMS data from 2016-2018, searching for events with two Z bosons (decaying to four leptons) and a photon.
result: Evidence of ZZγ production and observation of 4ℓγ, with cross-section measurements consistent with Standard Model predictions.
conclusion: These measurements provide important tests of the Standard Model and constraints on anomalous triple and quartic gauge couplings.

title: Monte Carlo Event Generation With Continuous Normalizing Flows
authors: E. Bothmann, T. Janßen, M. Knobbe, B. Schmitzer, And F. Sinz
abstract:
Author(s): E. Bothmann, T. Janßen, M. Knobbe, B. Schmitzer, and F. Sinz

We apply continuous normalizing flows trained with the flow matching method to the problem of phase-space sampling in Monte Carlo event generation for high-energy collider physics. Focusing on lepton-pair and top-quark pair production with multiple jets, the two computationally most expensive proces…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 091902] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies continuous normalizing flows trained with flow matching to phase-space sampling in Monte Carlo event generation for high-energy collider physics.
motivation: The authors aim to address the computational cost of phase-space sampling in Monte Carlo event generation for processes like lepton-pair and top-quark pair production with jets.
method: They use continuous normalizing flows with the flow matching training method to efficiently sample the phase-space.
result: The method demonstrates improved sampling performance for the most computationally expensive processes.
conclusion: The work shows the potential of generative models, particularly normalizing flows, in high-energy physics event generation, though it is not related to the specified research interests.

title: Coherently Enhanced Radiation Friction In Laser-Plasma Collisions
authors: E. G. Gelfer, A. M. Fedotov, M. P. Malakhov, O. Klimo, And S. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): E. G. Gelfer, A. M. Fedotov, M. P. Malakhov, O. Klimo, and S. Weber

We reconsider the footprints of radiation friction in a head-on collision of a bunch of relativistic charged particles with a laser pulse by demonstrating that forward and backward radiation and radiation friction are coherently enhanced in a dense bunch. This opens an avenue to observe radiation fr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 095001] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates coherently enhanced radiation friction in dense relativistic particle bunches colliding with laser pulses.
motivation: To understand and potentially observe radiation friction effects in laser-plasma interactions.
method: The authors reconsider radiation friction dynamics in head-on collisions, accounting for coherent enhancement in dense bunches.
result: They demonstrate that forward and backward radiation and radiation friction are coherently enhanced in dense bunches, offering a new avenue for observing radiation friction.
conclusion: The coherent enhancement could enable experimental observation of radiation friction in laboratory laser-plasma setups.

title: Noise-Induced Replicator Dynamics In Evolutionary Games
authors: Guocheng Wang, Qi Su, Long Wang, And Joshua B. Plotkin
abstract:
Author(s): Guocheng Wang, Qi Su, Long Wang, and Joshua B. Plotkin

In evolutionary game theory, the interplay between strategic evolution and environmental stochasticity gives rise to new dynamical regimes, with implications in fluctuating social, ecological, and economic environments.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 097401] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how environmental stochasticity affects evolutionary game dynamics, leading to new dynamical regimes.
motivation: To understand how noise influences strategic evolution in fluctuating environments, with implications for social, ecological, and economic systems.
method: Analyzes replicator dynamics under environmental stochasticity, likely using mathematical models and possibly simulations.
result: Identifies new dynamical regimes arising from the interplay between strategic evolution and noise.
conclusion: Noise can fundamentally alter evolutionary outcomes, highlighting the importance of considering environmental fluctuations in game theory.

title: Spin Waves Without Spin Waves: A Case For Soliton Propagation In Starling Flocks
authors: Andrea Cavagna, Guido Cimino, Javier Cristín, Matteo Fiorini, Irene Giardina, Angelo Giustiniani, Tomás S. Grigera, Stefania Melillo, Roberto A. Palombella, Leonardo Parisi, Antonio Ponno, Mattia Scandolo, And Zachary S. Stamler
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Cavagna, Guido Cimino, Javier Cristín, Matteo Fiorini, Irene Giardina, Angelo Giustiniani, Tomás S. Grigera, Stefania Melillo, Roberto A. Palombella, Leonardo Parisi, Antonio Ponno, Mattia Scandolo, and Zachary S. Stamler

Collective turns in starling flocks propagate linearly with negligible attenuation, indicating the existence of an underdamped sector in the dispersion relation. According to linear response theory, beside granting linear propagation of the phase perturbations, the real part of the frequency should …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 098301] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective turns in starling flocks as soliton propagation, using analogies with spin waves but focusing on nonlinear dynamics.
motivation: To explain the linear propagation of collective turns in starling flocks and the lack of damping.
method: They analyze the dispersion relation and propose soliton-like solutions to account for underdamped propagation.
result: They find that soliton propagation, rather than linear spin waves, better explains the observed collective behavior.
conclusion: The study suggests that nonlinear excitations govern collective motion in bird flocks.

title: Ab Initio Short-Range Nuclear Matrix Elements For Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay
authors: A. Todd, T. Shickele, A. Belley, L. Jokiniemi, And J. D. Holt
abstract:
Author(s): A. Todd, T. Shickele, A. Belley, L. Jokiniemi, and J. D. Holt

We present converged ab initio calculations of short-range neutrinoless double-beta ([MATH])-decay nuclear matrix elements for the key experimental isotopes [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. Starting from different nuclear forces derived from chira…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 092501] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: Ab initio calculations of short-range nuclear matrix elements for neutrinoless double-beta decay in several isotopes.
motivation: To accurately predict the half-life of neutrinoless double-beta decay, which is crucial for searching for physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Using different nuclear forces from chiral effective field theory, they perform ab initio calculations of the short-range part of the matrix elements.
result: They achieve converged results for key isotopes, showing the significance of short-range contributions.
conclusion: The short-range matrix elements are essential for accurate predictions of neutrinoless double-beta decay rates.

title: Collective Magnetic Excitations In A Photoexcited Electron-Doped Cuprate Superconductor
authors: Daniel Jost, Jiarui Li, Jordyn Hales, Jonathan Sobota, Giacomo Merzoni, Leonardo Martinelli, Shuhan Ding, Ke-Jun Xu, Justine Schlappa, Andreas Scherz, Robert Carley, Benjamin E. van Kuiken, Teguh C. Van Kuiken, Teguh C. Asmara, Le Phuong Hoang, Laurent Mercadier, Sergii Parchenko, Martin Teichmann, Patrick S. Kirchmann, Giacomo Ghiringhelli, Brian Moritz, Zhi-Xun Shen, Thomas P. Devereaux, Yao Wang, and Wei-Sheng Lee

The first time-resolved observation of collective magnetic excitations in a photoexcited cuprate across energy, momentum, and time proves that light-induced paramagnon dynamics cannot be explained by simple thermalization.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 096502] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: 首次时间分辨观察光激发电子掺杂铜氧化物超导体中的集体磁激发，证明其动力学不能由简单热化解释。
motivation: 研究光激发下超导体中的磁激发行为，以理解非平衡态下的物理机制。
method: 使用时间分辨光谱技术，结合能量、动量和时间分辨测量。
result: 观察到光诱导的paramagnon动力学，排除了简单热化模型。
conclusion: 光激发下的磁激发行为非热化，可能涉及更复杂的非平衡过程。

title: Diffusive Noise Controls Early Stages Of Genetic Demixing
authors: Rashmiranjan Bhutia, Stephy Jose, Prasad Perlekar, And Kabir Ramola
abstract:
Author(s): Rashmiranjan Bhutia, Stephy Jose, Prasad Perlekar, and Kabir Ramola

Theoretical descriptions of the stepping-stone model, a cornerstone of spatial population genetics, have long overlooked diffusive noise arising from migration dynamics. We derive a fluctuating hydrodynamic description of this model from microscopic rules, which we then use to demonstrate that diffu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 098401] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a fluctuating hydrodynamic description of the stepping-stone model in spatial population genetics, demonstrating that diffusive noise from migration controls early genetic demixing.
motivation: Existing theoretical descriptions of the stepping-stone model neglect diffusive noise arising from migration dynamics, which may be crucial for accurate predictions.
method: The authors derive a fluctuating hydrodynamic description from microscopic rules and use it to analyze the influence of diffusive noise on genetic demixing.
result: They show that diffusive noise plays a significant role in the early stages of genetic demixing, affecting the dynamics beyond deterministic descriptions.
conclusion: Including diffusive noise is essential for a complete understanding of spatial population genetics, as it alters the early-time behavior of the system.

title: Electron Loss And Target Excitation In keV-energy Proton Collisions With B And ${\mathrm{C}}^{+}$
authors: N. W. Antonio, I. B. Abdurakhmanov, A. Espinosa-Gayosso, And A. S. Kadyrov
abstract:
Author(s): N. W. Antonio, I. B. Abdurakhmanov, A. Espinosa-Gayosso, and A. S. Kadyrov

The one-center Coulomb–Sturmian convergent close-coupling method is applied to proton collisions with the boron atom and singly charged carbon ion. Here we report an update to our target-structure implementation, in which configuration state functions are constructed using the method of coefficients…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022829] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies an updated one-center Coulomb-Sturmian convergent close-coupling method to compute electron loss and target excitation cross sections in keV-energy proton collisions with boron and carbon ions.
motivation: Accurate modeling of ion-atom collision processes is important for astrophysical and fusion plasma applications.
method: The method uses the one-center Coulomb-Sturmian convergent close-coupling approach, with an improved target-structure implementation based on configuration state functions built via coefficients.
result: Provides updated cross-section data for electron loss and target excitation for proton collisions with B and C+.
conclusion: The enhanced method improves accuracy, and the results are relevant for modeling plasma and astrophysical environments.

title: Double And Triple Photoionization Of The Be-like ${\mathrm{B}}^{+}$ Ion: Role Of double-$K$-shell-vacancy States
authors: A. Müller, P.-M. Hillenbrand, S.-X. Wang, S. Schippers, S. Reinwardt, M. Martins, J. Seltmann, F. Trinter, I. Bray, D. V. Fursa, And A. S. Kheifets
abstract:
Author(s): A. Müller, P.-M. Hillenbrand, S.-X. Wang, S. Schippers, S. Reinwardt, M. Martins, J. Seltmann, F. Trinter, I. Bray, D. V. Fursa, and A. S. Kheifets

Double and triple photoionization of Be-like [MATH] ions have been studied in the photon-energy range from approximately 250 to 1300 eV. The method of merged photon and ion beams was employed and calculations were performed in support of the experiments making use of different theoretica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023110] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies double and triple photoionization of Be-like B+ ions, focusing on the role of double-K-shell-vacancy states.
motivation: To understand correlated multi-electron processes and the influence of inner-shell vacancies in atomic photoionization.
method: Experimental merged photon-ion beam measurements in the 250-1300 eV range, supported by theoretical calculations.
result: Measured cross sections for double and triple photoionization, revealing contributions from double-K-shell-vacancy resonances.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of double-K-shell-vacancy states in multiple photoionization of Be-like ions.

title: Excitation Function Of Detachment With Simultaneous Target Ionization In Slow Collisions Of ${\mathrm{D}}^{−}$ With He And Ar
authors: M. Schulz, F. Herrmann, W. Zhang, A. B. Voitkiv, B. Najjari, M. Siddiki, A. Dorn, M. Grieser, F. Grussie, H. Kreckel, O. Novotny, A. Wolf, T. Pfeifer, C. D. Schröter, And R. Moshammer

Author(s): M. Schulz, F. Herrmann, W. Zhang, A. B. Voitkiv, B. Najjari, M. Siddiki, A. Dorn, M. Grieser, F. Grussie, H. Kreckel, O. Novotny, A. Wolf, T. Pfeifer, C. D. Schröter, and R. Moshammer

We have measured momentum analyzed electrons and singly charged recoil ions ejected in slow collisions of [MATH] ions with He and Ar in triple coincidence with neutralized projectiles. From the data, we extracted relative triple differential cross sections for detachment and detachment w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022823] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: Measured momentum-analyzed electrons and recoil ions from slow D- collisions with He and Ar to extract relative triple differential cross sections for detachment and detachment with simultaneous target ionization.
motivation: Investigate the dynamics of negative ion detachment and target ionization in slow ion-atom collisions.
method: Triple coincidence measurements of electrons, recoil ions, and neutralized projectiles.
result: Extracted relative triple differential cross sections for detachment and detachment with simultaneous target ionization.
conclusion: Provides experimental data on these collision processes.

title: Manipulation Of Temporal Cavity Solitons In Pulsed-driving Kerr Fiber Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Zhibin Ren, Benli Yu, And Zhiqiang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Zhibin Ren, Benli Yu, and Zhiqiang Wang

Temporal cavity solitons (CSs), recognized for their exceptional stability and controllability, hold great promise as information carriers in all-optical storage and processing systems. Pulsed driving serves as an effective strategy to boost the pump-to-soliton conversion efficiency and optimize CS …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023522] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the manipulation of temporal cavity solitons in pulsed-driving Kerr fiber resonators for all-optical storage and processing.
motivation: Temporal cavity solitons are promising optical information carriers, but their manipulation and efficiency need improvement.
method: The authors use pulsed driving in Kerr fiber resonators to enhance pump-to-soliton conversion efficiency and control soliton dynamics.
result: The study demonstrates improved manipulation and optimization of temporal solitons in this configuration.
conclusion: The findings support the potential of pulsed-driving Kerr resonators for all-optical information storage and processing.

title: Femtosecond Chiroptical Switching Mediated By A Geometric Phase
authors: Yang Liu, Peipei Ge, Yueming Zhou, Xiaosong Zhu, Min Li, And Peixiang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Liu, Peipei Ge, Yueming Zhou, Xiaosong Zhu, Min Li, and Peixiang Lu

The authors propose a femtosecond chiroptical switch in atomic hydrogen that maps the otherwise unobservable global phase of a Rabi‑oscillating system onto the chirality of a bound electron wave packet. They demonstrate that this global phase is dominated by a geometric phase accumulated during cyclic evolution on the Bloch sphere, which endows the switch with high robustness against variations in the control‑pulse area.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L021102] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: 该论文提出了一种在原子氢中通过几何相位实现飞秒手性开关的方案，将Rabi振荡系统的全局相位映射到束缚电子波包的手性上。
motivation: 探索将不可观测的全局相位以可观测的方式表现出来，并利用其鲁棒性实现光开关。
method: 利用Rabi振荡系统在Bloch球上的循环演化累积几何相位，并对手性电子波包进行操纵。
result: 演示了该手性开关对控制脉冲面积变化具有高鲁棒性。
conclusion: 基于几何相位的手性开关为飞秒光控提供了一种新方法，但不在指定研究方向的范围内。

title: Phonon-induced Hypersensitive Transitions In Lanthanide Double Perovskites
authors: Muyi Zhang, Sakarn Khamkaeo, Xinyi Cai, Utkarsh Singh, Pedram Pakmehr, Kunpot Mopoung, Yuxuan Li, Julia Morat, Kirill Chernenko, Antti Kivimäki, Wei-Xin Ni, Maths Karlsson, Irina A. Buyanova, Weimin M. Chen, Sergei I. Simak, Igor A. Abrikosov, Yuttapoom Puttisong, And Feng Gao

Author(s): Muyi Zhang, Sakarn Khamkaeo, Xinyi Cai, Utkarsh Singh, Pedram Pakmehr, Kunpot Mopoung, Yuxuan Li, Julia Morat, Kirill Chernenko, Antti Kivimäki, Wei-Xin Ni, Maths Karlsson, Irina A. Buyanova, Weimin M. Chen, Sergei I. Simak, Igor A. Abrikosov, Yuttapoom Puttisong, and Feng Gao
