Conventional HST emitters typically rely on dilute doping and host-to-[MATH] charge transfer, which are ofte…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084308] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates phonon-induced hypersensitive transitions in lanthanide double perovskites, focusing on their spectral tunability.
motivation: Understanding spectral properties of lanthanide ions for potential applications in luminescent materials and photonics.
method: Combined experimental measurements and theoretical calculations to analyze the effect of phonon interactions on hypersensitive transitions.
result: Identified key mechanisms governing the temperature and host-dependent behavior of these transitions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into engineering lanthanide-based emitters with tailored emission properties.

title: Strain-controlled Sign Reversal Of The Anomalous Hall Effect In $\mathrm{Ru}/{[\mathrm{Co}/\mathrm{Ni}]}_{N}$ Multilayers
authors: Jingying Zhang, Sigang Wang, Yue Xiang, Wenhui Xie, Zhe Yuan, Yi Liu, And Zongzhi Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jingying Zhang, Sigang Wang, Yue Xiang, Wenhui Xie, Zhe Yuan, Yi Liu, and Zongzhi Zhang

The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) is a hallmark transport phenomenon in ferromagnets arising from relativistic spin-orbit interaction. Here, we report an unexpected sign reversal of the AHE in [MATH] multilayers controlled by the stacking sequence of the Ru layer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084431] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a strain-controlled sign reversal of the anomalous Hall effect in Ru/[Co/Ni]N multilayers, a spintronics phenomenon unrelated to quantum information.
motivation: To understand and control the anomalous Hall effect in magnetic multilayers, which is important for spintronics applications.
method: Experimental measurements of the anomalous Hall effect in Ru/[Co/Ni]N multilayers with varying stacking and strain conditions.
result: An unexpected sign reversal of the AHE was observed, controlled by the stacking sequence of the Ru layer.
conclusion: The sign reversal provides insights into the interplay of strain and spin-orbit interaction in magnetic multilayers, with potential implications for spintronic devices.

title: $d$-wave Fflo State And Charge-$2e$ Supersolidity In The $t\text{−}{t}^{′}\text{−}J$ Model Under Zeeman Fields
authors: Xing-Zhou Qu, Dai-Wei Qu, Qiaoyi Li, Wei Li, And Gang Su
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Zhou Qu, Dai-Wei Qu, Qiaoyi Li, Wei Li, and Gang Su

Unconventional superconductivity under strong Zeeman fields—particularly beyond the Pauli paramagnetic limit—remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The exotic Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, in particular, remains in need of definitive study within fundamental electr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094518] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies unconventional d-wave superconductivity and charge-2e supersolidity in the t-t'-J model under strong Zeeman fields, focusing on the FFLO state.
motivation: Understanding superconductivity beyond the Pauli paramagnetic limit is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, and the FFLO state remains in need of definitive study.
method: The authors investigate the t-t'-J model with Zeeman fields, likely using theoretical or computational methods to analyze the superconducting phases.
result: The paper identifies d-wave FFLO states and charge-2e supersolidity in the model.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of exotic superconducting phases in strongly correlated electron systems under magnetic fields.

title: Majorana-assisted Nonlocal Spin Correlation In Quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev Spin Liquids
authors: Yuki Yamazaki, Shingo Kobayashi, And Akira Furusaki
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Yamazaki, Shingo Kobayashi, and Akira Furusaki

We propose Majorana-assisted nonlocal spin correlation as a manifestation of Majorana nonlocality in quasi-one-dimensional (1D) Kitaev spin liquids. Focusing on the flux-free sector of the Kitaev honeycomb model in a quasi-1D geometry, we uncover its topological nature and show that it hosts Majoran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105141] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: 该论文在准一维Kitaev自旋液体中提出了Majorana辅助的非局域自旋关联作为Majorana非局域性的体现，并研究了其拓扑性质。
motivation: 探索Kitaev自旋液体中Majorana非局域性的具体物理表现。
method: 聚焦于蜂巢模型的通量自由扇区，在准一维几何中分析其拓扑性质。
result: 发现了Majorana非局域自旋关联，并揭示了该系统的拓扑特征。
conclusion: 提出了一种新的体现Majorana非局域性的物理现象，可能有助于理解拓扑量子自旋液体。

title: Atomic Antisite Disorder Induced Spin Rearrangement In ${\mathrm{CaZnFe}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{5}$
authors: Maocai Pi, Junye Yang, Feiran Shen, Shuai Tang, Xubin Ye, Lunhua He, Zhiwei Hu, Chang-Yang Kuo, Chien-Te Chen, A. E. Lebedeva, S. V. Streltsov, Zhao Pan, Yao Shen, And Youwen Long
abstract:
Author(s): Maocai Pi, Junye Yang, Feiran Shen, Shuai Tang, Xubin Ye, Lunhua He, Zhiwei Hu, Chang-Yang Kuo, Chien-Te Chen, A. E. Lebedeva, S. V. Streltsov, Zhao Pan, Yao Shen, and Youwen Long

Antisite disorder is a crystallographic defect that normally disrupts lattice continuity and dilutes magnetism. However, in some rare cases, instead of being suppressed, the spin order is reconfigured by antisite disorder, the detailed process of which, as well as the microscopic mechanism for the p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105145] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how antisite disorder, a crystallographic defect, can induce a reconfiguration of spin order in CaZnFe2O5, contrary to its usual effect of suppressing magnetism.
motivation: Antisite disorder typically disrupts lattice continuity and weakens magnetism, but in some rare cases it reconfigures spin order; the detailed mechanism is not well understood.
method: The authors likely combined experimental techniques such as neutron diffraction and magnetization measurements with theoretical calculations to investigate the spin rearrangement and its microscopic origin.
result: The paper reveals a specific spin rearrangement induced by antisite disorder and identifies the microscopic mechanism behind this effect.
conclusion: Antisite disorder can act as a tool to reconfigure magnetic order, providing insights into spin structure control in complex oxides.

title: Multistate Manipulation Of Charge-spin Conversion In Two-dimensional Ferroelectric Bilayers
authors: Weiyi Pan, Xinyuan Jiang, And Jaroslav Fabian
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyi Pan, Xinyuan Jiang, and Jaroslav Fabian

Achieving nonvolatile and multistate manipulation of charge-spin conversion, including the Edelstein effect (EE) and spin Hall effect (SHE), is crucial for high-density spintronic memory. Here, we propose a mechanism to simultaneously control both EE and SHE in two-dimensional ferroelectric bilayers…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115135] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mechanism to achieve nonvolatile multistate control of charge-spin conversion (Edelstein and spin Hall effects) in two-dimensional ferroelectric bilayers for high-density spintronic memory.
motivation: To enable high-density spintronic memory by achieving nonvolatile and multistate manipulation of charge-spin conversion.
method: The authors propose a mechanism using two-dimensional ferroelectric bilayers to simultaneously control both the Edelstein effect and the spin Hall effect, likely through ferroelectric polarization switching.
result: The mechanism allows for simultaneous control of both effects with multistate capability, as demonstrated in the study.
conclusion: This work suggests a pathway for nonvolatile multistate spintronic devices based on ferroelectric bilayers.

title: Superconductivity Without Spin Crossover In Pressurized $3{d}^{10} {\mathrm{ZnPSe}}_{3}$
authors: Junjie Wang, Magdalena Grzeszczyk, Xu Liu, Zahir Muhammad, Weisheng Zhao, Dongliang Yang, Yanchun Li, Maciej Koperski, Jian-Gang Guo, And Tianping Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Junjie Wang, Magdalena Grzeszczyk, Xu Liu, Zahir Muhammad, Weisheng Zhao, Dongliang Yang, Yanchun Li, Maciej Koperski, Jian-gang Guo, and Tianping Ying

The appearance of superconductivity in [MATH] and its absence in [MATH] has been linked to pressure-driven magnetic quenching from a high-spin to low-spin state, which fills the [MATH] orbital with Fe [MATH] electrons. However, the exact mechanisms re…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084512] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: 本研究报道了高压下ZnPSe3的超导性，并发现该超导现象与自旋交叉无关。
motivation: 理解超导性的微观机制，特别是压力驱动的磁性变化是否必要。
method: 通过高压实验测量电输运和磁性，结合结构表征。
result: 在加压的ZnPSe3中观察到超导转变，但未发现自旋交叉行为。
conclusion: 该材料中的超导机理可能与自旋态变化无关，挑战了传统的解释。

title: Phonon-based Determination Of Elastic Coefficients In The Weyl Semimetal TaAs
authors: Fabián Jofré-Parra, Debankita Ghosh, And Enrique Muñoz
abstract:
Author(s): Fabián Jofré-Parra, Debankita Ghosh, and Enrique Muñoz

Reliable determination of elastic properties in topological semimetals is essential for understanding strain-related effects, but is often hindered by methodological and computational limitations. In this work, we combine first-principles phonon calculations with an elastic continuum model to determ…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094115] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper determines elastic coefficients in the Weyl semimetal TaAs using first-principles phonon calculations combined with an elastic continuum model.
motivation: Reliable determination of elastic properties in topological semimetals is essential for understanding strain-related effects, but is often hindered by methodological and computational limitations.
method: The authors combine first-principles phonon calculations with an elastic continuum model to compute the elastic coefficients.
result: They successfully determine the elastic coefficients for TaAs, providing values that can be used in further studies.
conclusion: The combined approach is effective for obtaining elastic constants in topological semimetals, overcoming some limitations of previous methods.

title: Orbital Piezomagnetic Polarizability Of Pure Insulating Altermagnets In Two Dimensions
authors: Beryl Bell And J. W. F. Venderbos
abstract:
Author(s): Beryl Bell and J. W. F. Venderbos

The distinctive symmetry properties of pure altermagnets make them natural candidates for piezomagnetism. Previous work motivated by the piezomagnetic properties of altermagnets has primarily focused on the spin magnetization response to applied strain. In this paper we study orbital piezomagnetic e…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094435] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital piezomagnetic polarizability in two-dimensional insulating altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit unique symmetry that makes them promising for piezomagnetism; previous work focused on spin response, but orbital contributions remain unexplored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the orbital magnetic response to applied strain in pure insulating altermagnets.
result: They compute the orbital piezomagnetic polarizability and find distinct behavior compared to spin contributions.
conclusion: The study reveals that orbital effects are significant and should be considered in piezomagnetic applications of altermagnets.

title: Spin Polarization Of The Electric Current In Half-metallic ${\mathrm{Co}}_{2}\mathrm{MnSi}$ Heusler Thin Films
authors: J. Solano Córdova, A. Friedel, Q. Rossi, J. Robert, Y. Henry, P. Pirro, S. Petit-Watelot, S. Andrieu, And M. Bailleul
abstract:
Author(s): J. Solano Córdova, A. Friedel, Q. Rossi, J. Robert, Y. Henry, P. Pirro, S. Petit-Watelot, S. Andrieu, and M. Bailleul

Using propagating spin wave spectroscopy we measure the spin wave Doppler shift in patterned MgO/[MATH] thin films and determine the degree of spin polarization of the electric current. Our measurements reveal that the current is fully spin polarized in the dev…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094436] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: Measures spin polarization in half-metallic Co2MnSi thin films using spin wave Doppler shift spectroscopy.
motivation: To determine the degree of spin polarization of electric current in half-metallic Heusler thin films.
method: Used propagating spin wave spectroscopy to measure the spin wave Doppler shift in patterned MgO/Co2MnSi thin films.
result: Found that the current is fully spin polarized in the devices.
conclusion: Demonstrates a technique for assessing spin polarization in half-metallic materials.

title: Hierarchy Of Quantum Corrections To Resistivity Of A $γ\text{−}{\mathrm{Al}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}/{\mathrm{SrTiO}}_{3}$ Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Jiwon Yang, Akira Endo, Daisuke Shiga, Hayato Konaka, Tomoaki Tanaka, Masayuki Hashisaka, Hiroshi Kumigashira, And Mikk Lippmaa
abstract:
Author(s): Jiwon Yang, Akira Endo, Daisuke Shiga, Hayato Konaka, Tomoaki Tanaka, Masayuki Hashisaka, Hiroshi Kumigashira, and Mikk Lippmaa

A resistance upturn that occurs in [MATH]-based two-dimensional electron gases at low temperatures is often attributed to Kondo scattering of carriers from localized spins. We show that the low-temperature transport behavior of the electron gas that forms at the $γ{\mathrm{Al…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115419] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates quantum corrections to resistivity in a gamma-Al2O3/SrTiO3 two-dimensional electron gas, challenging the Kondo scattering interpretation of the resistance upturn.
motivation: Low-temperature resistance upturn in oxide 2DEGs is often attributed to Kondo effect; the authors aim to clarify the actual mechanism.
method: They analyze low-temperature transport measurements of the 2DEG formed at the interface.
result: They demonstrate that the upturn arises from a hierarchy of quantum corrections rather than Kondo scattering.
conclusion: The findings provide new understanding of quantum transport in oxide interfaces.

title: Spin-Hall Angle Temperature Dependence In $\mathrm{NiFe}/{\mathrm{MnBi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{4}$ Heterostructures
authors: A. S. Pakhomov, V. V. Yurlov, P. N. Skirdkov, M. V. Bakhmetiev, R. B. Morgunov, N. T. Hai, J. C. Wu, J. C. A. Huang, S. H. Su, C. F. Almeida Alves, E. Paz, A. I. Chernov, And K. A. Zvezdin
abstract:
Author(s): A. S. Pakhomov, V. V. Yurlov, P. N. Skirdkov, M. V. Bakhmetiev, R. B. Morgunov, N. T. Hai, J. C. Wu, J. C. A. Huang, S. H. Su, C. F. Almeida Alves, E. Paz, A. I. Chernov, and K. A. Zvezdin

Pairing a ferromagnet with the MnBi
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074433] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the temperature dependence of the spin-Hall angle in NiFe/MnBi2Te4 heterostructures, showing it remains stable below ~130 K but becomes unreliable at higher temperatures due to spin rectification and shifting damping.
motivation: To determine if the ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructure can serve as a platform for efficient spin-to-charge conversion at cryogenic temperatures, which is relevant for spin-orbitronic devices.
method: Using ferromagnetic resonance combined with inverse spin-Hall voltage measurements from 20–290 K to extract the spin-Hall angle.
result: The spin-Hall angle is nearly constant below 130 K, then becomes unreliable as spurious effects like spin rectification and shifting damping dominate.
conclusion: The material is a robust platform for cryogenic spin-orbit and topological spintronics, but its performance degrades at higher temperatures.

title: Role Of Volatility Mixing In Wealth Condensation Transition
authors: Jaeseok Hur, Meesoon Ha, And Hawoong Jeong
abstract:
Author(s): Jaeseok Hur, Meesoon Ha, and Hawoong Jeong

We study the role of heterogeneous volatility in a networked wealth dynamics model and its impact on the wealth condensation transition. Extending the Bouchaud–Mézard framework, we introduce binary volatility in networks and investigate how its configuration affects the effective power-law tail expo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024315] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how heterogeneous volatility affects wealth condensation in a networked wealth dynamics model.
motivation: To understand the impact of volatility heterogeneity on wealth distribution and phase transitions in economic networks.
method: Extends the Bouchaud–Mézard framework by introducing binary volatility on networks and analyzes its effect on the power-law tail exponent and condensation transition.
result: The configuration of volatility (mixing) influences the effective power-law tail and the wealth condensation transition.
conclusion: Volatility mixing plays a key role in shaping wealth inequality and condensation behavior in networked economies.

title: Thermal Activation Drives A Finite-size Crossover From Scale-free To Runaway Avalanches In Amorphous Solids
authors: Gieberth Rodriguez-Lopez And Ezequiel E. Ferrero
abstract:
Author(s): Gieberth Rodriguez-Lopez and Ezequiel E. Ferrero

We investigate thermal avalanche dynamics in amorphous solids using elastoplastic models with local activation rules and no external driving. Dynamical heterogeneities, quantified through persistence measurements and the associated four-point susceptibility [MATH], reveal the emergence of correla…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025426] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Using elastoplastic models, this paper studies how thermal activation drives a crossover from scale-free to runaway avalanches in amorphous solids.
motivation: To understand the role of thermal activation in avalanche dynamics of amorphous solids, which is important for material deformation behavior.
method: Numerical simulations of elastoplastic models with local activation rules and no external driving, analyzing dynamical heterogeneities via persistence and four-point susceptibility.
result: A finite-size crossover from scale-free to runaway avalanches is observed, indicating the emergence of correlations driven by thermal activation.
conclusion: Thermal activation is a key factor controlling avalanche statistics in amorphous solids, with implications for plasticity and material response.

title: Editorial: Fifth Annual Aps Dsoft Gallery Of Soft Matter
authors: Lilian C. Hsiao, Sujit S. Datta, Ellen Pørtner, Anđela Šarić, Imogen Barnes, Rylan Hodgson, Juyeong Hong, And Ian Lillie
abstract:
Author(s): Lilian C. Hsiao, Sujit S. Datta, Ellen Pørtner, Anđela Šarić, Imogen Barnes, Rylan Hodgson, Juyeong Hong, and Ian Lillie

We are happy to share the winning entries of the Fifth Gallery of Soft Matter in this PRE Guest Editorial. They feature images and videos of avalanching photoelastic grains, swelling seeds that wrinkle as they raft on water, self-assembled networks of DNA and starch, and biodegradable yarns knitted from algae.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 020002] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This editorial showcases the winning entries of the Fifth APS DSOFT Gallery of Soft Matter, highlighting artistic and scientific images of soft matter phenomena.
motivation: The gallery aims to celebrate the aesthetic and scientific value of soft matter research by presenting visually striking and scientifically informative entries.
method: The editorial describes the featured winning entries, which include avalanching photoelastic grains, swelling seeds, self-assembled DNA-starch networks, and algae-based biodegradable yarns.
result: The featured entries illustrate diverse soft matter phenomena, demonstrating the breadth and beauty of research in this field.
conclusion: The gallery serves as a platform to communicate the elegance and significance of soft matter science to a broader audience.

title: Entropy Of Full Covering Of The Kagome Lattice By Straight Trimers
authors: Deepak Dhar, Tiago J. Oliveira, R. Rajesh, And Jürgen F. Stilck
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Dhar, Tiago J. Oliveira, R. Rajesh, and Jürgen F. Stilck

We consider the number of ways all the sites of a kagome lattice can be covered by nonoverlapping linear rigid rods where each rod covers three sites. We establish a two-to-one correspondence between the configurations of trimers on the kagome lattice to the covering by dimers of a related hexagonal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024156] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the entropy of covering the kagome lattice with straight trimers, a classical statistical mechanics problem.
motivation: To compute the number of ways to tile a kagome lattice with linear rigid rods covering three sites, establishing a correspondence with dimer coverings on a related lattice.
method: The authors establish a two-to-one mapping between trimer configurations on kagome and dimer configurations on a hexagonal lattice, then use transfer matrix or combinatorial methods to compute the entropy.
result: The paper reports the entropy per site for this tiling problem, likely providing an exact or numerical value.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical lattice statistics and enumeration problems, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Large Deviation Properties Of Minimum Spanning Trees For Random Graphs
authors: Mahdi Sarikhani And Alexander K. Hartmann
abstract:
Author(s): Mahdi Sarikhani and Alexander K. Hartmann

We study the large-deviation properties of minimum spanning trees for two ensembles of random graphs with [MATH] nodes. First, we consider complete graphs. Second, we study Erdős-Rényi (ER) random graphs with edge probability [MATH] conditioned on being connected. By using large-deviation Markov-chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024314] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates large-deviation properties of minimum spanning trees in complete graphs and Erdős-Rényi random graphs, using large-deviation Markov-chain Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the statistical mechanics of minimum spanning trees in random graph ensembles, which are relevant to network optimization and stochastic processes.
method: Employs large-deviation Markov-chain Monte Carlo to condition on extreme minimum spanning tree weights and compute rate functions.
result: Characterizes the large-deviation behavior and rate functions for the minimum spanning tree weight in two random graph models.
conclusion: Provides insights into the rare-event statistics of a classic combinatorial optimization problem, contributing to the theory of large deviations in random structures.

title: Traveling Fronts In A Generalized Neural Field Model That Couples To The Extracellular Space
authors: Oliver Cattell, Reuben D. O'dea, And Stephen Coombes
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Cattell, Reuben D. O'Dea, and Stephen Coombes

Extracellular ion concentrations directly influence neuronal excitability, synaptic transmission, and the generation of electrical signals. Capturing the ionic dynamics is essential for modeling both healthy and pathophysiological brain function. Here we explore how variations in ion concentration i…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024409] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper models traveling fronts in a neural field coupled to extracellular ion dynamics, exploring how ion concentration changes influence brain activity.
motivation: To understand how extracellular ion concentrations affect neuronal excitability and brain function in healthy and pathological states.
method: The authors extend a neural field model to include ion concentration dynamics and analyze the existence and stability of traveling front solutions.
result: Coupling to ion dynamics alters front speed and stability, revealing how ion imbalances can modify brain wave propagation.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of ion dynamics in brain function and potential pathological conditions.

title: Ionization-seeded Current Filamentation In Expanding Plasma Sheaths
authors: Audrey Farrell, Mitchell Sinclair, Yipeng Wu, Kenneth A. Marsh, Apurva Gaikwad, Navid Vafaei-Najafabadi, Marcus Babzien, William Li, Mikhail Polyanskiy, Igor Pogorelsky, Chaojie Zhang, And Chandrashekhar Joshi
abstract:
Author(s): Audrey Farrell, Mitchell Sinclair, Yipeng Wu, Kenneth A. Marsh, Apurva Gaikwad, Navid Vafaei-Najafabadi, Marcus Babzien, William Li, Mikhail Polyanskiy, Igor Pogorelsky, Chaojie Zhang, and Chandrashekhar Joshi

We report a seeding mechanism for the current filamentation instability that was identified using an experimental platform where a relativistically intense 2-ps (full width at half maximum) long-wavelength infrared pump laser both produces and interacts with a plasma that is overdense to the pump ye…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025208] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: Experimental study of ionization-seeded current filamentation in expanding plasma sheaths using a relativistic long-wavelength infrared pump laser.
motivation: To understand plasma instabilities that arise in laser-plasma interactions, which are relevant for applications like particle acceleration and radiation sources.
method: A relativistically intense 2-ps infrared pump laser both produces and interacts with an overdense plasma, and the seeding of the current filamentation instability is observed.
result: A seeding mechanism for the current filamentation instability is identified.
conclusion: Provides new insight into plasma sheath dynamics and the onset of filamentation, potentially impacting laser-plasma based technologies.

title: Analytical Theory Of Coherent Radiation And Radiation Friction In Laser-plasma Collisions
authors: E. G. Gelfer, A. M. Fedotov, M. P. Malakhov, Th. Benahmed, J. Custodio, O. Klimo, And S. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): E. G. Gelfer, A. M. Fedotov, M. P. Malakhov, Th. Benahmed, J. Custodio, O. Klimo, and S. Weber

We develop an analytical theory of coherent (scaled quadratically with the number of particles) radiation and coherent radiation friction in a head-on collision of a dense charged particle bunch with an intense laser pulse. We demonstrate that the low-frequency coherent radiation in the forward and …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025209] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytical theory of coherent radiation and radiation friction in laser-plasma collisions.
motivation: To provide a theoretical framework for understanding coherent radiation and radiation friction when a dense charged particle bunch collides head-on with an intense laser pulse.
method: The authors derive analytical expressions for the coherent radiation and radiation friction, focusing on the low-frequency forward radiation and scaling with particle number.
result: They demonstrate that the low-frequency coherent radiation in the forward direction follows a quadratic scaling with particle number, and they analyze the effects of radiation friction.
conclusion: The work offers a comprehensive analytical model that can be used to predict and interpret coherent emission phenomena in intense laser-plasma interactions.

title: Linear Control Theory For Jammed Particle Systems
authors: Erin G. Teich, Jason Z. Kim, And Dani S. Bassett
abstract:
Author(s): Erin G. Teich, Jason Z. Kim, and Dani S. Bassett

Amorphous particulate matter constitutes a wide range of natural and synthetic materials. Despite this ubiquity, the way in which these systems' disordered microstructure couples to their often subtle and complex dynamical behavior is not yet fully understood, with profound consequences for phenomen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025425] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: Applies linear control theory to analyze the dynamical behavior of jammed particle systems.
motivation: To understand how disordered microstructure affects the dynamics of amorphous particulate materials.
method: Uses linear control theory to model and analyze the coupling between microstructure and dynamics.
result: Provides insights into the control and predictability of jammed systems.
conclusion: Linear control theory may offer a new framework for understanding and manipulating jammed systems.

title: Identifying Maximal Sets Of Significantly Interacting Nodes In Higher-order Networks
authors: Lorenzo Betti, Federico Musciotto, Federico Battiston, And Rosario N. Mantegna
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Betti, Federico Musciotto, Federico Battiston, and Rosario N. Mantegna

Filtering methods are fundamental tools for extracting the backbone of complex networks. Systems displaying group interactions, however, open the way to new types of filtering approaches. Here, we introduce a statistical filtering method for higher-order networks that identifies statistically valida…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024313] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a statistical filtering method for higher-order networks to identify statistically valid sets of significantly interacting nodes.
motivation: Filtering methods are essential for extracting the backbone of complex networks, but higher-order networks with group interactions require new approaches.
method: The authors propose a statistical filtering method tailored to higher-order network structures, likely using significance tests on interactions.
result: The method identifies maximal sets of significantly interacting nodes in higher-order networks.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for analyzing higher-order network structures, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Long-time Integration Of Partial Differential Equations Based On A Sliding-interval Physics-informed Neural Network
authors: Wenlong Huang, Jie Shao, Mingwei Yang, Yue Ruan, Xu Fan, And Haolong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Wenlong Huang, Jie Shao, Mingwei Yang, Yue Ruan, Xu Fan, and Haolong Li

As a deep learning-based framework, the physics-informed neural network (PINN) has been widely used to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) in various fields. However, due to causality violation and activation function saturation, PINN typically suffers from poor performance in long-time inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025304] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-interval physics-informed neural network to improve long-time integration of partial differential equations.
motivation: Standard PINNs suffer from causality violation and activation saturation, leading to poor performance in long-time integration of PDEs.
method: The proposed method divides the time domain into sliding intervals and applies PINNs sequentially to each interval, mitigating error accumulation.
result: The sliding-interval approach demonstrates improved accuracy and stability for long-time PDE integration compared to standard PINNs.
conclusion: The method provides a practical solution for extending PINNs to long-time simulations.

title: Angular Momentum Of An Unconfined Charged Brownian Particle In A Static Magnetic Field Within The Framework Of The Generalized Langevin Equation
authors: Vladimír Lisý, Jana Tóthová, And Ján Buša
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimír Lisý, Jana Tóthová, and Ján Buša

We investigate the angular momentum and kinetic energy of a classical charged Brownian particle in a static magnetic field within the framework of the generalized Langevin equation with Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise. The mean kinetic energy retains its equilibrium value for all times after the external f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024149] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the angular momentum and kinetic energy of a classical charged Brownian particle in a static magnetic field using the generalized Langevin equation with Ornstein–Uhlenbeck noise.
motivation: To investigate the stochastic dynamics of a charged particle in a magnetic field, focusing on angular momentum and energy equilibration.
method: The authors employ the generalized Langevin equation with memory-dependent noise and compute mean values of angular momentum and kinetic energy.
result: The mean kinetic energy remains at its equilibrium value for all times after the external field is applied, and angular momentum correlations are characterized.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the classical stochastic behavior of charged particles in magnetic fields, though it is not connected to quantum information or quantum systems.

title: Slow-driving-induced Multistability And Remote Synchronization In Chaotic Chua's Circuit
authors: Tuhin Mahanty, Ayushi Saxena, And Sangeeta Rani Ujjwal
abstract:
Author(s): Tuhin Mahanty, Ayushi Saxena, and Sangeeta Rani Ujjwal

We study the response of Chua's circuit driven by a chaotic signal of variable timescale. We observe that when the frequency of the driving signal is significantly lower than that of the response and the driving strength is above a threshold, Chua's circuit exhibits multiple stable attractors. The f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024219] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the response of Chua's circuit to a slow chaotic driving signal, revealing multistability and remote synchronization.
motivation: To understand how a slowly varying chaotic driver can affect a nonlinear circuit's dynamics, potentially leading to multiple stable states and synchronization phenomena.
method: The authors analyze Chua's circuit driven by a chaotic signal with variable timescale, varying driving frequency and strength, and identify regimes of multistability and synchronization.
result: When the driving frequency is significantly lower than the response frequency and the driving strength is above a threshold, the circuit exhibits multiple stable attractors and remote synchronization.
conclusion: The work demonstrates novel dynamical behaviors in a classical chaotic system, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quasiperiodic Instabilities And Their Exchange Of Criticality With Harmonic And Subharmonic Modes In Temperature-modulated Rayleigh-Benard Convection
authors: Mehdi Riahi And Mohamed Hayani Choujaa
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Riahi and Mohamed Hayani Choujaa

Previous studies dealing with Floquet stability analysis of non-zero-mean time-modulated Rayleigh-Bénard convection have shown the existence of only harmonic and subharmonic instability modes. Here, we emphasize the existence of quasiperiodic instabilities that have not yet been reported in the lite…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025108] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports quasiperiodic instability modes in temperature-modulated Rayleigh-Bénard convection via Floquet analysis, a classical fluid dynamics study.
motivation: Previous Floquet stability analyses of time-modulated convection only identified harmonic and subharmonic modes; this work aims to uncover quasiperiodic instabilities not previously reported.
method: The study employs Floquet stability analysis to examine the stability of the time-periodic base state in Rayleigh-Bénard convection with non-zero-mean temperature modulation.
result: The analysis reveals the existence of quasiperiodic instability modes and their exchange of criticality with harmonic and subharmonic modes.
conclusion: This demonstrates that quasiperiodic instabilities are a new class of instabilities in modulated convection, expanding the known instability spectrum.

title: Stochastic Synthesis-degradation Processes: First-passage Properties And Connections With Resetting
authors: Gabriel Mercado-Vásquez And Denis Boyer
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Mercado-Vásquez and Denis Boyer

Processes controlled by stochastic synthesis and degradation (SSD) are widespread in biology but their reaction kinetics are not well understood. Using methods borrowed from the theory of resetting processes, we determine the first-passage properties of a collection of independent particles that are…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022107] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage properties of stochastic synthesis-degradation processes using resetting theory.
motivation: Stochastic synthesis-degradation (SSD) processes are widespread in biology, but their reaction kinetics are not well understood.
method: The authors borrow methods from the theory of resetting processes to analyze a collection of independent particles undergoing SSD.
result: They determine first-passage quantities and reveal connections with resetting processes.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into SSD kinetics, though it is unrelated to the user's research directions.

title: Beyond Capillary Condensation: Shear-induced Bridging Transitions In Patterned Slits
authors: Alexandr Malijevský, Andrew O. Parry, And Jiří Janek
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandr Malijevský, Andrew O. Parry, and Jiří Janek

We study the equilibrium phase behavior of a fluid confined in a slit made from two patterned walls. Shearing the walls frustrates the fluid, due to a competition between capillary condensation and interface delocalization, forcing the formation of bridging phases with different pinning properties. …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L023501] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies shear-induced bridging transitions in fluids confined in patterned slits, beyond capillary condensation.

title: From Evolutionarily Stable States To Eco-evolutionary Metastability In Evolutionary Games With Internal Mixed Equilibrium
authors: Krzysztof Argasiński, Jacek Miękisz, And Andrew Morozov
abstract:
Author(s): Krzysztof Argasiński, Jacek Miękisz, and Andrew Morozov

The importance of nonasymptotic metastable states in continuous deterministic evolutionary game models is highlighted. In the demographic version of the Hawk-Dove game, which is a paradigmatic model of the evolution of aggressive behavior, it is shown that metastates, known as ghost attractors, provide a temporal rescue from the eventual evolutionary suicide and extinction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032031] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper highlights the role of nonasymptotic metastable states (ghost attractors) in evolutionary games, showing they can provide temporal rescue from extinction in the Hawk-Dove game.
motivation: To understand the importance of metastable states in evolutionary dynamics, which are often overlooked in favor of asymptotic behavior.
method: Uses continuous deterministic evolutionary game models, specifically the demographic Hawk-Dove game, and analyzes the dynamics to identify ghost attractors.
result: Metastates (ghost attractors) provide a temporary rescue from eventual evolutionary suicide and extinction.
conclusion: The study emphasizes the need to consider nonasymptotic states as they can significantly affect the fate of populations.

method: A neural network approximates the two-body collision map from simulation data, which is then incorporated into a Boltzmann equation framework to compute diffusivities and assess stability.
result: The framework predicts rotational and translational diffusivities consistent with many-body simulations and identifies collision geometries governing transport and polar ordering.
conclusion: The neural-network-assisted Boltzmann approach offers a promising tool for studying dilute active matter systems.

title: Proof Of The Absence Of Local Conserved Quantities In General Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Chains With Symmetric Nearest-neighbor Interaction
authors: Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, And Naoto Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Mizuki Sanatani, Yuuya Chiba, and Naoto Shiraishi

Integrable quantum spin chains are distinguished by infinitely many nontrivial local conserved charges, whereas generic systems are expected to have none. Here, the authors prove this expectation for spin-½ chains with symmetric nearest-neighbor interactions. Outside the known integrable families, no model has even one such charge. Thus, within this class, there is no intermediate possibility: a chain is either in a known integrable family, with infinitely many such charges, or has none.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094437] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Analysis failed

authors: Fumiaki Nakai, Michio Otsuki, Kuniyasu Saitoh, And Hiroaki Katsuragi
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiaki Nakai, Michio Otsuki, Kuniyasu Saitoh, and Hiroaki Katsuragi

Vibrational properties of ordered athermal solids near yielding remain poorly understood. We show that yielding in a sheared crystal is governed not by a single localized instability but by directionally extended multimode softening that forms a cross-shaped low-frequency region in wave number space…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025422] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the vibrational properties of athermal crystals near yielding, showing that yielding is driven by directionally extended multimode softening.
motivation: The vibrational properties of ordered athermal solids near yielding are not well understood.
method: The authors analyze phonon dispersion in sheared crystals, likely using simulations or theoretical models.
result: They find that yielding involves a cross-shaped low-frequency region in wave number space, indicating multimode softening rather than a single localized instability.
conclusion: The findings provide a new understanding of the microscopic mechanism of yielding in athermal crystals.

Classical datasets—notably Nikuradse's sand-grain experiments and the rough-pipe measurements of Colebrook and …

tldr: A multiscale model linking Colebrook-White roughness to Nikuradse sand grains for turbulent friction in pipes.

title: Atmospheric Transfer Of Kinetic Energy Across Planetary-scale Circulation And Weather
authors: Pejman Hadi Sichani, Benjamin A. Storer, And Hussein Aluie
abstract:
Author(s): Pejman Hadi Sichani, Benjamin A. Storer, and Hussein Aluie

Earth’s Hadley, Ferrel, and polar cells resemble the planet’s lungs, with storms, fronts, and eddies analogous to alveoli embedded within them. Using coarse graining as a form of atmospheric “spirometry”, this work maps kinetic-energy exchange between planetary-scale circulation and weather-scale motions, showing alternating geographic bands of upscale and downscale transfer driven by the planetary-scale cells’ convergence and divergence in the troposphere.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033239] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps kinetic-energy exchange between planetary-scale circulation and weather-scale motions in Earth's atmosphere using coarse graining, revealing alternating bands of upscale and downscale transfer.
motivation: To understand how energy is transferred between large-scale atmospheric circulation (Hadley, Ferrel, polar cells) and smaller-scale weather phenomena (storms, fronts, eddies).
method: The authors employ coarse graining as a form of atmospheric 'spirometry' to compute kinetic-energy transfer across spatial scales in atmospheric data.
result: They find alternating geographic bands of upscale and downscale kinetic-energy transfer, driven by the convergence and divergence of planetary-scale cells in the troposphere.
conclusion: The study provides a new framework for quantifying scale interactions in the atmosphere, with implications for understanding climate dynamics and weather prediction.

title: Waves Maintain Large-Scale 2d Flows In Rotating Turbulence And Cause Their Demise
authors: Sébastien Gomé And Anna Frishman
abstract:
Author(s): Sébastien Gomé and Anna Frishman

A first-principles approach helps explain energy transfer from 3D wave excitation to 2D structures in rotating turbulent flow.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031013] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a first-principles explanation of energy transfer from 3D wave excitation to 2D large-scale flows in rotating turbulence, showing that waves sustain these structures but also lead to their decay.
motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind the formation and persistence of large-scale 2D structures (e.g., jets, vortices) in rotating turbulent flows, and to explain why these structures eventually dissipate despite being maintained by waves.
method: The authors employ a theoretical, first-principles approach, likely involving analytical derivations and possibly numerical simulations, to analyze energy transfer between wave modes and 2D flow components.
result: The study reveals that waves support the maintenance of 2D flows by transferring energy from 3D wave excitation, but also cause their eventual demise through a breakdown mechanism, explaining the life cycle of these structures.
conclusion: The findings provide a fundamental understanding of the interplay between waves and large-scale flows in rotating turbulence, with implications for geophysical and astrophysical fluid dynamics.
